# ...Preface...

**T**HIS edition of Carroll's Statutes is a compilation of all laws of a general and permanent nature in force in Kentucky, January 1st, 1922.

The work has been entirely re-edited, revised, annotated and brought to date. All legislation has been given its permanent place and the annotations are as recent as Volume 191 Kentucky Reports. References have been given to the Kentucky Reports, Southwestern Reporter, Kentucky Law Reporter and the Kentucky Opinions. Many valuable annotations have been made from cases reported in the Kentucky Opinions, which cases are not to be found reported elsewhere.

Great care has been exercised in editing this edition of the Kentucky Statutes. In addition to the very valuable work of Judge John D. Carroll, has been added the exhaustive "Notes to Statutes" of Judge Charles B. Seymour, which notes have been re-edited and distributed under the sections of this edition to which they apply.

The index has been carefully revised and enlarged. The numerous changes made in the statutes have required a very complete revision. Titles have been multiplied and a special effort has been made to include not only technical titles but also those of a popular character. Many cross references have been used and it is believed the index will be found to be the most complete ever made of the statute law of Kentucky.

Acknowledgement is gratefully rendered to Mr. Henry Pirtle for valuable assistance in the preparation of the text and to Judge Charles B. Seymour whose "Notes to Statutes" have added greatly to the value of the annotations in this edition.

This work represents a long cherished ambition of the editors and publishers to present to the profession in one volume all the statute law of a general and permanent nature in force in Kentucky, accompanied by thorough annotations and a complete index. It is hoped the work will prove of service to those who will have occasion to use it.

WILLIAM EDWARD BALDWIN.

Louisville, Kentucky,
January 1, 1922.

BILL OF RIGHTS
That thegreatand essentialprinciplesof
liberty and free government may be recog-
nized and established. We declare that :
§1 . Inherentand inalienablerights.-
All men are,by nature,freeand equal,and
have certain inherent and inalienable
rights, among which may be reckoned :
1. The rightof enjoyingand defending
their lives and liberties .
2. The rightof worshipping Almighty
God according to the dictatesof their con-
sciences .
3. The right of seeking and pursuing
theirsafety and happiness.
4. The right of freelycommunicating
theirthoughts and opinions.
5. The rightof acquiringand protecting
property .
6. The right of assembling together in
a peaceable manner for theircommon good ,
and of applying to those invested with the
power of government for redressof griev-
ances or other proper purposes, by peti-
tion, address or remonstrance .
7. The right to bear arms in defense of
themselves and of the state subject to the
power of the general assembly to enact
laws to prevent persons from carrying con-
cealed weapons .

CHAPTER 1 .
Act July 3, 1893 .
ACTIONS .
§1 . Incest; fornication; adultery; for
chargeof. A charge of incest, fornication
oradulteryagainst a female shallbe action-
able; and in such cases the plaintiffshall
not be held to allegeor prove specialdam-
ages .
§1 . Who may maintain the action. The stat-
ute of 1811 (4 Litt. 385) authorized a man to
maintain the action. Morris v . Barkley , 1 Litt.
64; Phillips v . Wiley , 2 Litt. 153.
Words within meaning of statute. To say a
female " is a drunken whore " is to accuse her of
fornication or adultery. Williams v . Greenwade ,
3 Dana 432. And so for a man to say of a woman
that he has had sexual intercourse with her .
Adams v . Rankin , 1 Duv . 58. Charge of fornica-
tion is actionable without proof of malice . Nich-
olson v . Dunn , 21 R. 643 ; 52 S. W. 935 ; and see
Morris v .Curtis,20 R. 56 ; 45 S. W. 86 .
SEYMOUR'S NOTES
The word " bitch " in an accusation does not
come within this section. Craig v . Pyles , 101 Ky .
593, 18 R. 1043 , 39 S. W. 33; Peters v . Garth , 20
R. 1934 , 50 S. W. 682 .
Malice does not mean or imply personal malice ,
but simply a wrongful act done without just cause
or excuse . Louisville Press Co. v . Tennelly , 105
Ky . 365 , 20 R. 1231 , 49 S. W. 15.
An insane delusion on the subject to which the
slanderous words related is a complete defense to
the action under this section. Irvine v .Gibson , 117
Ky . 306 , 25 R. 1418 , 77 S. W. 1106 .
Certain words charged unchastity .
White , 188 Ky . 153, 221 S. W. 528 .

§ 2. Seduction; action for.--Action for
seduction may be maintained without any
allegation or proof of the loss of service
of the female by reason of the wrongful
act of the defendant .
The
§ 2. Common law remedy is not repealed by
the statute. The father may sue for the seduction
of his daughter by the common law for loss of
service and incidental expenses , or by the statute
authorizing him to sue for seduction. Wilhort v.
Hancock ,5 Bush 567 ; Pence v . Dozier , 7 Bush 133 .
Female can not sue for her seduction .
statute gives the right of action to those only

§ 12. Construction of statute .- Statute does not
change the common law form of proceeding , or
authorize a joint action for several trespasses,

could take judgment against all for the damages .

1 J. J. M. 360. Without a common intent and
co-operation there can be no joint liability in
the commission of trespass. Bonte v . Postell, 109
Ky . 64 ; 22 R. 583 ; 58 S. W. 536 .

or several assessment of damages in an action

" is intended as a complete and uniform system

supervision over the " licensing and regulation of dogs ."
Said act legislates generally upon the licensing, use ,
" regulation" and keeping of dogs , the right of private
persons to kill dogs under certain circumstances , the
daties of officers where dogs have been chasing deer and
game , dogs found off the owner's premises , etc. In the
case of Buchannon v . Commonwealth , 95 Ky . 334 , 25
8. W. 265 , 15 R. 738 , it was held that a certain act
was " intended to be a complete system of statutory law
relating to crimes and punishments , and as a conse-
quence to supersede or repeal all existing statutes on that
subject." As that latter act included only part of a
former law the parts not so included were held to have
been repealed , rather than to be in force as amended inthe new law . It is believed that this view of the pur-
pose of the legislature to enact " a complete system " for
the licensing and regulation of dogs and the protection
of live stock from ravages by dogs thereby repeals all
former laws on the same subject except so far as spe-
cifically kept in force therein . These exceptions are
specificallyset forth in the section above quoted - relating
to disposal of mad or diseased dogs and dogs chasing
deer , etc. subjects thus brought into relation to the new
licensing " system."For the reasons given it is believed that so much of
the broad rights given in section 68 as were not fully
covered by sections 68a -5 and 68a -9 were repealed by
the new " system " of sections 68b -1, et seq., and the
whole of said section 68 is therefore omitted .- Ed .

It would not seem open to serious doubt that the
provisions of the act of 1893 forming section 68 , pro-
viding that the owner of a dog should be liable for the
damage done by it, may reasonably be held to have been
included in the title. Assuming that the same provis-
ions of the act of 1906 forming section 68a -5 could

annon case quoted in the said note would not this whole
act of 1906 - excepting alone section 68a -9 concerning

this point section 68a -5 has not been omitted from this
compilation preceding a decision on the question.

SEYMOUR'S NOTES
This section was intended to authorize the
refunding to tax collectorswho have paid in more
than was due from them , but does not authorize
an auditor to investigate the claims of individuals
that taxes were wrongfully collected from them ,
and refund to individuals taxes wrongfully col-
lected. County v.Bosworth ,160 Ky .312,169 S. W.
742 .
This section does not authorize an action by a
taxpayerto compeltheauditorto issuea warrant
for a portion of the taxes paid upon insurance
premiums , in excess of the amount actually due ,
since the purpose of the section is to authorize
a refund to tax collectorswho have paid in more
than was due from them . Bosworth v . Metro-
politan Life Ins. Co., 162 Ky . 344, 172 S. W. 661 .
This section does not authorize the state
auditor to correct erroneous assessments , but to
correct mistakes made by collectingofficers. Louis-
villeGas & ElectricCo. v. Bosworth, 169 Ky .
824, 185 S. W. 125.
Mandamus proceeding to compel the auditor
of public accounts to draw his warrant for the
refund of money improperlypaid for taxes, isnot
a " suit against the state," but merely a pro-
ceeding against an officerto compel the per-
formance of a statutory duty . Louisville Gas &
Electric Co. v . Bosworth , 169 Ky . 824 , 185 S. W.
125 .
A corporation paid a license tax under the
mistaken belief that it was liable therefor . Man-
damus rightly issued against the auditor to draw
warrant to repay same . There had been no assess-
ment of the tax. Greene v . E. H. Taylor & Sons ,
184 Ky . 739 , 212 S. W. 925 .
This section does not authorize the auditor to
return to a taxpayer taxes paid by mistake . A
tax paid by mistake when no tax was owing, is
not recoverable, if the commonwealth and itsofficers had no means of coercing payments .
Greene v.Federal Coal Co.,184 Ky .664,212 S. W.
580 .

Historical sketch of the manner the
boundary was formed and finallyfixed.
§186m . Historicalsketch.- The bound-
aryof the stateof Kentucky is to be ascer-
tained-
1. By reference to the deed of cession of
territorynorthwest of the Ohio riverby the
commonwealth of Virginia to the congress
of the United States, dated the firstday of
March , 1784 .
2. By the act of the Virginialegislature,
known as the " Compact with Virginia,"
entitled" An act concerningthe erection
of the Districtof Kentucky into an inde-
pendentState," passedtheeighteenthday
of December , 1789.
3. By the act of the Virginia legislature
of1776,by which thecountyof Fincastle
was divided,and threeadditionalcounties
established, viz.: Kentucky , Washington
and Montgomery .
4. By reference to arrangements made
between Virginia and Kentucky , and be-
tween Kentucky and the stateof Tennessee.
The legislatureof Virginia,in the organ-
izationof countieson the western border of
the state,prior to the act of cession, never
gave them a definiteboundary westwardly ,
but leftthem to be bounded by the western

ry, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-

teries and burying -grounds , as aforesaid,

§ 202. Cemetery companies ; bonds and notes
owned by , are subject to taxation . Com . v . Lex .
Cem . Co., 114 Ky . 165 ; 24 R. 924 ; 70 S. W. 280 ;
and see Con ., § 170 .
§ 203. Penalty for failingto report.-
Failure on the part of any board of direc-
tors or trustees of cemeteries and burying-
grounds , incorporated by the laws of this
commonwealth , to make said report, as
herein specifiedin this act, shallbe guilty

§204. Additionalpenalty. For each
succeeding day thereaftershallbe deemed
and considered a separate offense, and the
same fine shall be imposed and collected

made as herein provided for.

fines.- The penalty and finesimposed by
this act shall be enforced and collected as
other penalties and fines and forfeitures are
enforced and collected in this common-
wealth.

port ineligible.- Boards of directors or
trustees, as aforesaid, failing to comply
with this act shall become ineligible to
serve as directors or trustees in the said
corporation as aforesaid.

§ 209. Champertous contract ; attorney . The
fact that a party prosecuting a suit has agreed
to give his attorney one -half of amount recovered
is not available as a defense to the defendant .
The contract is only void as between the plaintiff
and the attorney . A champertous contract, unless
it relates to real estate, does not deprive the
creditor of his right to collect his debt . Wehm-
boff v . Rutherford , 98 Ky . 91 ; 17 R. 659 ; 32 S. W.
298 .
SEYMOUR'S NOTES
The vendor who retains a purchase lien on
property may agree to assist the purchaser in a
suit for the value of timber cut by trespassers
from the land, in considerationthat he is to
have an agreed portion of the recovery applied
on the purchase notes . Hall v . Deaton , 24 R. 314 ,
68 8. W. 672 .
The possession of the life tenant is not adverse
to the estate of the remainder man . Davis v .
Wilson . 115 Ky . 639 , 25 R. 21 , 74 S. W. 696 .
By this statute a champertous agreement is
made null and void, but the cause of action, out
of which it grows , is not affected. Cumb , Tel. &
Tel. Co. v . Maxberry , 134 Ky . 642, 121 S. W. 447.
An attorney may be Kable on a contract for
assistance rendered him in preparing a case ; but
if the contract be contingent on success it will
not be enforcible. Lynn v . Moss , 139 Ky . 637 ,
23 R. 214, 62 S. W. 712 .
The opinion in this case states that a stranger
to a contract cannot attack its validity on the
ground of champerty . The question, however , did
not arise in the case because the contract was not
in fact champertous . Aetna Life Ins. Co. v . Week ,
163 Ky . 37 , 173 S. W. 317 .

§ 317. Authorizing devises for charitable uses.
-Our statute is a substantial re-enactment of 43
Elizabeth , and should receive a construction simi-
lar to that given the English statute. A devise
will be upheld , not only when it is given for the
charitablepurposes specificallynamed in the stat-
ute, but when given for such other " charitable
or humane " purposes as are kindred to those
named . Ford v. Ford , 91 Ky . 572 ; 13 R. 183 ;
16 S. W. 451 .
Charitable or humane purposes .- A devise for
the erection of a monument over the graves of
testator'sfamily isa devisefor a human purpose.
91 Ky . 572 ; 13 R. 183 ; 16 S. W. 451.
Construing devise to charitable use. Intention
of testatormust be construed, just as in con-
struing any other provisionof his will; and if
the real objects of his bounty can be ascertained,
the devise will be enforced for their benefit, and
not allowed to fail for want of a trustee or other
person in whom the title may vest. Penick v.
Thom , 90 Ky . 665 ; 12 R. 613 ; 14 S. W. 830.
Definition of a charitable use .- Whatever is
given for the love of God , or for the love of our
neighbor , in the catholic and universal sense, is
a gift for charitableuses. Ford v. Ford, 91 Ky .
572 ; 13 R. 183 ; 16 S. W. 451 .
Description of beneficiary; uncertainty .- In-
stance where the corporate names of asylums for
whose benefit devise was claimed to have been
made were not preciselyrecitedin the will, yet
were held by the descriptionin the will and ex-
traneousfactsto be sufficientlyidentified. Cromie
v.LouisvilleOrphans ' Home , 3 Bush 365; and see
Crawford v. Thomas , 114 Ky . 484; 21 R. 1100; 54
S. W. 197; Chambers v. Higgins, 20 R. 1425; 49
S. W. 436; and casescitedin note to § 318. Greer
v . Synod S. P. C., 150 Ky . 155 ; 150 S. W. 16;
Green v. Fidelity Trust Co., 134 Ky . 311; 120
S. W. 283; Gerick v. Gerick, 158 Ky . 478; 165
S.W. 695; Comptonv. Moore, 156Ky. 544; 161
S. W. 540 .
Devise of income to be paid annually to the
trustees of Lagrange school districtfor the educa-
tion of poor children, and maintenance of a good
common school in said district is not void for
uncertainty. Leedsv. Shaw,82 Ky.79; 6 R.26.
Municipalitycan not act as trusteefor religious
purposes. City of Maysville v. Wood , 102 Ky.
263 ; 19 R. 1292 ; 43 S. W. 403 .
Parol dedication.- A dedication of land to pub-
lic purposes, or for a church, may be made by
parol and establishedby parol evidence. Griffey
v. Bryars, 7 Bush 471; McKinney v. Griggs, 5
Bush 401 .
Purrose contemplated by donation . If one
gives or dedicatesland for religiouspurposes,he
must be regarded as holding the legal title in
trust for the purposes contemplated by the gift

or dedication. Baptist Church v . Presbyterian
If one agrees in writing to dedicate land for
church purposes, he can not be required to con-
vey it for " church and school purposes ." McDan-
iel v . Watson , 4 Bush 234 .
Reversion because of failure of charitable
object. Where property is for a valuable and
sufficientconsiderationconveyed upon condition
that the grantee keep the property in repair, and
after reimbursing himself the amount of the
considerationpaid, appropriatethe profitsto a
charity, the grantor can not recoverthe property
from the grantee after he has been reimbursed
because of the failureof the charitable object.
Morrow v . Slaughter , 5 Bush 330 .
When a congregation, to whose use land hasbeen voluntarilyconveyed, ceases to use it for
the purpose for which the dedication was made ,
the land reverts to the grantor ; and if the non-
user happens before the contract to convey isexecuted , a fortiori, a conveyance can not be en-
forced. McDaniel v . Watson , 4 Bush 234 .
Sale or exchange of trust property .- Instance
where trusteesof property, devised to a church
for a parsonage, were held to have the right to
use or exchange it, under the authority of an
act of the General Assembly . Littell v . Wallace ,
80 Ky . 252 ; 3 R. 770 .
If property held for religioususes be exchanged
for other property , the latter must be held for
the same uses and subject to the same conditions
attached to the first. If church property is sold
for its debts, any surplus must be held as the
originalpropertywas . Harper v. Straws, 14 B. M.

§ 317. Authorizing devises for charitable uses.
-Our statute is a substantial re -enactment of 43
Elizabeth, and should receivea constructionsimi-
lar to that given the English statute. A devise
will be upheld, not only when it is given for the
charitablepurposes specificallynamed in the stat-
ute, but when given for such other " charitable
or humane " purposes as are kindred to those
named . Ford v. Ford , 91 Ky . 572 ; 13 R. 183 ;
16 S. W. 451 .
Charitable or humane purposes .- A devise for
the erection of a monument over the graves of
testator's family is a devise for a human purpose .
91 Ky . 572 ; 13 R. 183 ; 16 S. W. 451 .
Construing devise to charitable use. Intention
of testator must be construed , just as in con-
struing any other provisionof his will; and if
the real objects of his bounty can be ascertained,
the devise will be enforced for their benefit, and
not allowed to fail for want of a trustee or other
person in whom the titlemay vest. Penick v.
Thom , 90 Ky . 665 ; 12 R. 613 ; 14 S. W. 830.
Definition of a charitable use .- Whatever is
given for the love of God , or for the love of our
neighbor , in the catholic and universal sense, is
a gift for charitable uses. Ford v . Ford , 91 Ky .
572 ; 13 R. 183 ; 16 S. W. 451 .
Description of beneficiary; uncertainty .- In-
stance where the corporate names of asylums for
whose benefit devise was claimed to have been
made were not preciselyrecitedin the will, yet
were held by the descriptionin the will and ex-
traneousfactsto be sufficientlyidentified. Cromie
v . Louisville Orphans ' Home , 3 Bush 365 ; and see
Crawford v . Thomas , 114 Ky . 484 ; 21 R. 1100 ; 54
S. W. 197; Chambers v. Higgins, 20 R. 1425; 49
S. W. 436; and casescitedin note to $ 318. Greer
v. Synod S. P. C., 150 Ky . 155; 150 S. W. 16;
Green v. Fidelity Trust Co., 134 Kỵ . 311; 120
S. W. 283; Gerick v. Gerick, 158 Ky . 478; 165
S.W. 695; Comptonv.Moore, 156Ky. 544;161
S. W. 540 .
Devise of income to be paid annually to the
trustees of Lagrange school districtfor the educa-
tion of poor children, and maintenance of a good
common school in said district is not void for
uncertainty. Leedsv.Shaw,82 Ky.79; 6 R.26.
Municipality can not act as trustee for religious
purposes. City of Maysville v. Wood , 102 Ky .
263; 19 R. 1292 ; 43 S. W. 403 .
Parol dedication.- A dedication of land to pub-
lic purposes, or for a church, may be made by
parolandestablishedbyparolevidence.Griffeyv. Bryars, 7 Bush 471; McKinney v. Griggs, 5
Bush 401 .
Purpose contemplated by donation . If one
gives or dedicatesland for religiouspurposes, he
must be regarded as holding the legal titlein
trust for the purposes contemplated by the gift
dedication. Baptist Church v . Presbyterian
Church,18 В. М. 635.
or
If one agrees in writing to dedicateland for
church purposes, he can not be requiredto con-
vey itfor" church and schoolpurposes." McDan-
iel v. Watson , 4 Bush 234 .
Reversion because of failure of charitable
object. Where property is for a valuable and
sufficientconsiderationconveyed upon condition
that the grantee keep the property in repair, and
after reimbursing himself the amount of the
considerationpaid, appropriate the profitsto a
charity, the grantor can not recover the property
from the grantee after he has been reimbursed
because of the failure of the charitable object .
Morrow v. Slaughter, 5 Bush 330.
When a congregation, to whose use land has
been voluntarilyconveyed, ceases to use it for
the purpose for which the dedicationwas made ,
the land reverts to the grantor ; and if the non-
user happens before the contract to convey is
executed , a fortiori, a conveyance can not be en-
forced. McDaniel v. Watson , 4 Bush 234 .
Sale or exchange of trust property .- Instance
where trustees of property , devised to a church
for a parsonage, were held to have the right touse or exchange it, under the authority of an
act of the General Assembly. Littellv. Wallace ,
80 Ky . 252 ; 3 R. 770 .
If propertyheld for religioususes be exchanged
for other property, the lattermust be held for
the same uses and subject to the same conditions
attached to the first. If church property is sold
for its debts, any surplus must be held as the
originalpropertywas. Harperv.Straws,14 BВ. М.

Certain persons withdrew from a certain church ,

When a trust for a charitable purpose has
been created, the grantor of any beneficiary hav-
ing an interest in the subject of the gift has a
right to enforce by legal proceedings a carrying
outof thetrust. Tatev.Woodyard,145Ky .613,140 S. W. 1044 .
A deed to a master of a Masonic lodge of land
for the purpose of a lodge room , a Baptist church
and a graveyard , created a valid trust for charita-
ble purposes , at least so far as the church and
the graveyard were concerned . Tate v . Woodyard ,
145 Ky . 613 , 140 S. W. 1044.
A certain bequest for charitable purposes was
voidforuncertainty. Gerick'sExecutorv.Gerick,

Under this sectionand $ 323, the property of
a voluntary firecompany is not, upon dissolution
of the company , subjectto dispositionas charita-
ble property . Kash v . Strong , 165 Ky . 843 , 178
S. W. 1133 .
The provision in a will, " everything else I
own goes to charity," being uncertainin itspur-
pose as to the beneficiaries, an agreement of the
heirs that part of such property be used for
charity and benevolent purposes, giving one of
the heirs discretion as to the amount to be given
to each of such objects, was held void for uncer-
tainty. Simmon's Exr . v. Hunt , 171 Ky . 397, 188

Where land is conveyed in trustfor a Sunday

tian Church of Moreland , 171 Ky . 534, 188 S. W.
626 .

256 , 214 S. W. 878 .
Three bequests to charities in a certain will
were sufficientlydefinite and certain. Miller v .
Tatum , 181 Ky . 490, 205 S. W. 557.

ARTICLE I
Who deemed Citizens
§ 332. Persons born or naturalized in
United States.- All persons born or natu-
ralizedin the United States,and subject to
the jurisdiction thereof , and who reside in
the commonwealth of Kentucky , shall be
deemed citizens thereof .

a§ 332. Alien wife .- Naturalization being
personal privilege, the alien wife does not become
a citizen by the naturalization of her husband .
White v . White , 2 Met . 185 .
Children under the age of twenty -one , of per-
sons naturalized,shall,ifdwellingin thiscountry,
be considered as citizens of the United States .
Id .
Jurisdiction of courts to naturalize .- Power to
naturalize foreigners is conferred by Congress on
certain designated state courts. The Lexington
city court being a court of record, having a clerk
and seal, and being vested with a limited com-
mon -law jurisdiction, has authority to admit aliens
to citizenship. Morgan v . Dudley , 18 В. М. 693 .
The act of naturalization, required by act of
Congress , is a judicial act, and Congress can not
compel state courts to its exercise. But state
courts may exercise jurisdiction if not prohibited
by the exclusive jurisdictionof the federal courts.
Id .
ARTICLE II
Expatriation,how effected
§ 333. Declaration relinquishingcitizen-
ship; residence abroad ; war with foreign
power . Whensoever any citizen of this
state,by deed in writing,in the presence of,
and subscribed by , two witnesses, and
acknowledged or proved in the county
court of the county in which he resides, or
by open declaration made in such court and
entered of record , shall declare that he
relinquishes the character of a citizen of
this state, and shall depart out of the same
with the intention,in good faith, to remain
absent therefrom, such person shall, from
the time of hisdeparture,be consideredas
having exercised his right of expatriation,
so far as regards this state, and shallnot
thenceforth be deemed a citizenthereof.
When any citizenof this state shallreside
elsewhere , and , in good faith, become a cit-
izen of some other state of this Union , or
the citizen or subject of a foreign state or
sovereign, he shallnot,while the citizenof
another state, or the citizenor subject of a
foreignstateor sovereign,be deemed a citi-
zen of thisstate.No act of any citizenunder
this section shall have any effectif done
while the United States shall be at war with
a foreign power .
§ 333. Citizen may expatriate himself, with the
consent of his state, express or presumed . But no
act of legislationcan denationalize a citizen with-
out his concurrence. Burkett v. McCarty ,10 Bush
758 .

§334. Right to own , hold and transfer
property. An alien, not being an enemy ,
shall, after he has declared his intention to
become a citizen of the United States ,
according to the forms required by law , be
enabled to recover, inherit, hold, and pass
by descent, devise or otherwise, any inter-
estin realor personal property,in the same
manner as if he were a citizen of this com-
monwealth .
§ 334. Alien can not inherit except under stat-
ute . By the common law aliens can not inherit.
This law is in force here , except as modified by
statute. White v . White , 2 Met . 185 ; and see
Com . v . Newcomb , 109 Ky . 18 ; 22 R. 516 ; 58 S. W.
445 .
Under Rev. Stat . an alien friend who had re-
sided in this state two years might receive, hold ,
and pass any right to land within the common-
wealth during the continuance of his residence
after that period. Yeaker v . Yeaker , 4 Met . 33 .
Alien can take lands by purchase , though not
by descent, at common law ; or, in other words , he
can take by act of the party , but not by act
of law . 2 Met . 185 .

§ 424. Bond and oath of office.- Every
person who shall be elected or appointed

good sureties,to be approved by the judge
of the county court, payable to the com-
monwealth of Kentucky , conditioned that

well and truly perform all the duties
thereof . The bond shall be recorded in a
book kept for that purpose , and the fact
that the oath has been taken and bond exe-

shall, with the names of the sureties, be
entered on the records of the county court .
§ 424. Action in name of commonwealth .----
Suitsupon constables' bonds may be brought
in the name of the commonwealth , for the use
of the person injured. Com . v. Teal, 14 В. М. 29.

constable to whom an execution was unlawfully

in which he does not reside, yet if he give bond
as such , it is good as a common law bond . Com . V.
Teal, 14 B. М. 29 .
Custody of property ; degree of diligence.- In
arrestinga slave under a warrant charging him
with crime , it was held to be the duty of the
constable, while he retained the custody , to exer-
cise the diligence of an ordinarily prudent man .
Tudor v . Lewis 3 Met . 378 .
Liability for money collected.- Sureties are
liable for claims placed in the constable's hands
for collection, on which he might obtain and
executeprocess,or which he might officiallycollect
without further precept, but not for demands
which the constable could not officially collect.
Com . v . Sommers , 3 Bush 555 ; see also Com . v .
Peters , 4 Bush 403 ,

constablewithout suit, on claims placed in his
hands for collection before the bond was executed .
Boswell v . Sheriff, 8 Bush 97.

to appealfrom thejudgment. Mullinsv.Bullock,

CHAPTER 26
(Act of December 3 ,1892)
CONSTRUCTION OF STATUTES
§ 446. " State;'' ''U. S." and "any other
state ." In the construction of statutes the
following rules shall be observed, unless
such construction would be inconsistent
with the manifest intentof the legislature.
The word " state," when applied to a part
of the United States, shall be construed to
include the several territories thereof and
the District of Columbia . And the words
" United States ” shall be also construed to
include the district and territories afore-
said. And the words " any other state,"
shallbe held to include any stateor terri-
tory, and any foreign government or coun
try and the District of Columbia .
§ 446. Change of phraseology in revision of a
statute, where the old law has been settled by
adjudication, will not be considered a change of
the law unless such was the evident intention .
Overfield v . Sutton , 1 Met . 621 ; Allen v . Ramsey ,
1 Met . 635 ; Johnson v . Offutt, 4 Met . 19 ; and see
note 9 .
An intention to change a well settled rule of
law should clearly appear before the presumption
should be indulged in that such a change has
been produced by an act of the legislature. Lee v.
Forman , 3 Met . 114 ; 4 Met . 19 .
Constitutionality of statute.- All doubt as to
the constitutionalityof a statute must be resolved
in favor of itsvalidity. C. & O. R. R. Co. v .Barren
Co., 10 Bush 604 ; Collins v . Henderson , 11 Bush
74 .
Contemporaneous construction.- The practical
construction given to a statute through a long
period , and acquiesced in by all departments of
the government , should control the court in con-
struing it, although that construction may con-
travent the letter of the law . Harrison v . Com .,
83 Ky . 162 ; 7 R. 74 ; Barbour v . City of Lou . 83
Ky . 95 ; 7 R. 16 ; Pennington v . Woolfolk , 79 Ky .
13; 3 R. 42; Collinsv. Henderson, 11 Bush 74; C.
R. & S. R. T. P. R. R. v . Com . 96 Ky . 525 ; 16 R.
681; 29 S. W. 360 ; Auditor v . Cain , 22 R. 1888 ;
61 S. W. 1016 ; City of Lou . v . Lou . School Board ,
27 R. 209 ; 84 S. W. 729. Where boundary of city
was uncertain the lines as adopted and acted upon
by the property owners , as well as the city, for
more than twenty years should control. Belknap
v . City of Lou ., 93 Ky . 444 ; 14 R. 420 ; 20 S. W.
309 ; and where the provisions of the charter of
a turnpike company were ambiguous , the con-
struction given to it by the company , the public
and the officers of the county for many years is
adopted by the court. Clark's Run T. P. Co. v .
Com ., 96 Ky . 525 ; 16 R. 681 ; 29 S. W. 360 ; but if
the language of an act is certain its object can
not be defeated by any amount of contempor-
aneous interpretation. Com . v . Railroad Co., 95
Ky . 60 ; 15 R. 449 ; 23 S. W. 868.
Directory statute.- A statute is to be re-
garded as directory, if the directionsgiven by
the statute to accomplish a particularpurpose
may be violated and yet the object intended be
accomplished,leavingthe meritsof the case unaf-
fected. Varney v . Justice, 86 Ky . 596 ; 9 R. 743;
6 S. W. 457 .
Effect must be given to every provision of a
statute except in cases of absolute and irreconcil-
able incongruity. Dazey v . Killam , 1 Duv . 403 ;
Pendleton v. Pendleton, 6 Bush 469; and all the
provisionsmust be harmonized and enforced when
it ispracticable. C. & O. R. R. Co. v .Barren Co.,
10 Bush 604. Where the intent of a statute is
plain, the use of a word that would render the
act meaningless and absurd will be disregarded.
Bird v. Board of Commissioners, 95 Ky . 195; 15
R. 578; 24 S. W. 118; and every interpretationof
a statute that leads to an absurdity ought to be
rejected. Com . v. Hollidy,98 Ky .616; 17 R. 1159;
33 S. W. 943 .
Intention ; spirit. The spiritof the law and not
the letter should control in its construction, and
the object to be accomplished should be considered.
Harrison v . Com ., 83 Ky . 162 ; 7 R. 74 ; Bailey v.
Com ., 11 Bush 688; Com . v. Gale, 10 Bush 488;
Williams v. Com ., 78 Ky . 93; Barbour v. City of
Lou., 83 Ky . 95; 7 R. 16; Leonard v. Braswell, 99
Ky . 528 ; 18 R. 395 ; 36 S. W. 684 ; Bird v . Board
of Commissioners , 95 Ky . 195 ; 15 R. 578 ; 24 S. W.
118; Morrell RefrigeratorCo. v: Com ., 128 Ky .
447 ; 32 R. 1389 ; 108 S. W. 926 ; Com . v . Herald
Pub . Co., 128 Ky . 424; 32 R. 1293; 108 S. W.
892. But when the law is clear and explicitand
its provisionsare susceptibleof but one inter-
pretation, its consequences, if evil, can only be
avoided by legislativeaction, in changing the law.
Bosley v. Mattingly,14 B. M. 89; Com .v . Owens-
boro R. R. Co., 95 Ky . 60; 15 R. 449; 23 S. W.
868 .
Local and general law . It is held in Com . V.
Weller, 14 Bush 218,that the localoptionlaw didnot repealor affecta localact regulatingthe sale
of liquor, as the locallaw can be enforcedwithout
impairingthe efficacyof the generallaw. A gen-

§ 470. Frauds ; statute of; contracts
required to be in writing.- No action shall
be brought to charge any person-
1. For a representation or assurance
concerning the character, conduct , credit,
ability, trade,or dealings of another,made
with intent that such other may obtain
thereby credit,money or goods ; nor,
2. Upon a promise to pay a debt con-
tracted during infancy, or a ratificationof
a contract or promise made during infancy;
nor ,
3. Upon a promise of a personal repre-
sentativeas such to answer any liabilityof
his decedent out of hisown estate;nor,
4. Upon a promise to answer for the
debt, default, or misdoing of another ; nor,
5. Upon any agreement made in consid-
eration of marriage , except mutual
promises to marry ; nor,
6. Upon any contract for the sale of
real estate, or any lease thereof for longer
than one year ; nor ,
7. Upon any agreement which is not to
be performed within one year from the
making thereof, unless the promise, con-
tract, agreement , representation , assurance ,
or ratification, or some memorandum or
note thereof, be in writing, and signed by
the party to be charged therewith,or by his
authorized agent; but the consideration
need not be expressed in the writing; it
may be proved when necessary, or dis-
proved by parol or other evidence .

§ 524. Brands or labelsrequired; excep-
tion. All goods , wares and merchandise

marked as hereinafterprovided, and shall
not be exposed for sale in any place within

mark .

and where placed.- The brand, label or
mark hereby required shallcontain, at the
head or top thereof, the words " convict
made ," followed by the year and name of
the penitentiary, prison, reformatory or
other establishment in which it was made ,
in plainEnglishlettering, of the styleand
size known as great primer Roman con-
densed capitals. The brand or mark shall
in allcases,where the nature of the article
will permit, be placed upon the same,
and only where such branding or marking
isimpossibleshallitbe placedupon thebox
or other covering of the same , or be
attached to the article as a label . Said
brand or mark shall be placed upon the
most conspicuous part of the article or
itscovering, and said label, when used in-
stead of a brand or mark , shall be attached
in the most conspicuousplace.
§ 526. Dealing in unbranded goods;
removing or defacingbrand; penalties.-
It shallnot be lawfulfor any persondeal-
ing in thisstatein any such convict-made
goods,wares or merchandisemanufactured
in any state, except the state of Kentucky ,
knowingly to have the same in his posses-
sionforthe purposeof sale,or to offerthe
same for sale, without the brand , mark , or
label required by thisact, or to remove or
to deface such brand , mark or label. Any
person offending against the provisions of
this act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor ,
and , upon convictionthereof, shallbe sen-
tenced to pay a finenot exceeding fivehun-
dred dollars,or to be imprisoned for a term
not exceeding twelve months , or both, in
the discretionof the jury or court trying
the case.
§ 526a . Convict-mined coal and coke ;
penalty.- (1.) All coal mined or coke
manufactured by convict labor in any
state, and imported, brought, or intro-
duced intothe stateof Kentucky shall,dur-
ing shipment and beforebeing exposed for
sale,or used in any placewithinthisstate,
having a placard or label attached in a
conspicuous place to the car,barge or other
conveyance transporting such coal or coke ,
marked " convict-mined coal," or " convict-
made coke," in plain English bold-faced
lettering, not less than four inches in
height. And allvehiclesused in retailing
or conveying the same within this state
shall, in a similarmanner , be marked or
labeledina conspicuousplace.
(2.) It shallnot be lawfulfor any per-
son dealing in such convict-mined coal or
convict-made coke knowingly to have the
same in his possession for the purpose of
sale or use, or to offer the same for sale,
except under the conditions prescribed in
and by § 1 of thisact.
Any person offending against the provi-
sionsof thisact shallbe guiltyof a mis-
demeanor, and upon convictionthereof
shallbe sentencedto pay a finenot exceed-
ing fivehundred dollars, or to be impri-
soned for a term not exceeding twelve
months , or both , in the discretionof the
jury or courttryingthe case. (Thissection
is an act of April 29,1897.)

§ 809. Killing stock; fencing .- Where the
owner has not received compensation for fene-
ing, it is not necessary, to enable him to recover
one -half the loss sustained, that he should allege
or prove negligence. L. & N. R. R. Co. v.Belcher,

Where a railroad is lawfully inclosed the com
pany isliablefor injuryto stock strayingon the
rightof way , if caused by its negligence. 85 Ky .
151 ; 8 R. 896 ; 3 S. W. 10 ; Ky . Cent . R. R. Co. v .
Lebus , 14 Bush 518 .
Where stock straysupon a railroadfrom the
uninclosedlands of the owner , the company has
no remedy for the trespass, unless its road is
within a lawful inclosure, and it can not even
then recover damages for injury to its trains
if the accident was caused by negligently running
its cars over the stock . L. & N. R. R. Co. v . Sim-
mon , 85 Ky . 151 ; 8 R. 896 ; 3 S. W. 10.
The killing of stock is prima facie evidence
of negligence, and the burden is on the company
to show that the accident could not have been
avoided by the exercise of ordinary care. L. & N.
R. R. Co. v . Simmons , 85 Ky . 151 ; 8 R. 996 ; 3 S, W.
10 ; 13 Bush 475 ; and see L. & N. R. R. Co. v .
Jones , 21 R. 749 ; 52 S. W. 1116 ; M. & O. R. R.
Co. v . Roper ; 22 R. 666 ; 58 S , W. 518 .

§ 950-1 478COURTS OF JUSTICE
An appeal does not lie from an interlocutory
judgment which does not direct the payment of
money . Cummins v . Bradford , 5 Ky . Opinions 78 .
An order of court authorizing a plaintiff to
withdraw from the hands of an officerthe pro-
ceeds of attached property is a finaljudgment .
Rousseau v . Sheckler , 5 Ky . Opinions 282 .
A judgment confirmed a commissioner's report
of a settlement with an executor and dissolved an
injunction granted in the case and adjudged that
the money in the hands of the executor belonged
to him ; this was a finaljudgment . Roberts v . Ma-
lone, 5 Ky . Opinions 302.
The mere confirmation of a commissioner's
report of settlement was not a final judgment .
Sacra v. Bohannon's Admr ., 7 Ky . Opinions 548.
The court of appeals has jurisdiction of an
appeal from a judgment dismissing a petition
for divorce and refusing alimony . Graham v .
Graham , 8 Ky . Opinions 738 .
An order directing a party to pay money into
court is interlocutory; an order directingmoney
to be paid over to one of the parties is final.
Settle's Admr . v . Gordon , 8 Ky . Opinons 775 .
In an action of which it had no jurisdiction a
circuit court entered an order punishing for a
civilcontempt. The court of appeals awarded a
writ of prohibition against the enforcement of
the order. Union L., H. & P. Co. v. Tracy, Judge,
177 Ky . 662 , 197 S. W. 1175 .
The court of appeals has jurisdiction of an
appeal awarding an attorney a lien less than $200
on land for services in the action . Hatfield v .
Richmond , 177 Ky . 183 , 197 Ky . 654 .
The court of appeals has power to reviseand
correct a sentence of punishment for criminal
contempt if such sentence is illegalor imposes an
excessiveor cruelpunishment. Adams v.Gardner,
Judge , 176 Ky . 252 , 195 S. W. 412.
A county court has no jurisdictionto appoint
a receiver in an action to partition land or in
any other action . From such an order of the
county court no appeal lies to the court of ap-
peals. Cochran v . Simmons , 177 Ky . 562, 197 S. W.
930 , 178 Ky . 402 , 199 S. W. 66 .
An appeal was dismissed because the circuit
court had no jurisdiction to grant it; a cross
appeal was dismissed by the court of appeals.
Davis v . Davis , 178 Ky . 779, 199 S. W. 1075 .
Plaintiff recovered judgment cancelling a deed
of realty ; each of three defendants recovered a
judgmenton a counterclaimforlessthan$500,
but the three judgments together aggregated more
than $500 . The circuit court had no jurisdiction
to grant an appeal to plaintiff. Davis v. Davis,
178 Ky . 779 , 199 S. W. 1075 .
A money judgment was rendered by a circuit
court for more than $ 200 and less than $ 500 . A
party to the judgment fileda transcriptof the
record in the clerk's officeof the court of ap-
peals. The filing was treated as including a
motion for an appeal . Covington v . Sullivan, 172
Ky . 534 , 189 S. W. 709 ; Carter County Com . Bk .
v . Eifort, 179 Ky . 232 , 200 S. W. 342 ; Matney v .
Edmonds , 179 Ky . 243 , 200 S. W. 365 .
An appeal lay in a certain action for alimony
from an ordermaking an allowanceto support
the wife pending the action. Kelly v . Kelly , 179
Ky . 586 , 200 S. W. 925 .
Under this subsection and subsection 3 an ap-
peal to the court of appeals should be dismissed
where the amount in controversy is less than $ 500 ,
and it appears that neither the constitutional
question nor the validity of a statute is involved .
Gough v. Ill. Cent. R. R. Co., 166 Ky . 568, 179 S.
W. 449 .
Where the amount in controversy , exclusive
of interest and cost, exceeds $ 200 and is less than
$500 the supreme court may grant an appeal from
a judgment for recovery of money , if from the
record it appears that justice requires it, or where
the construction of the statute or a constitutional
provision is in issue. Louisville & N. R. R. Co. v.
Greenbrier Distillery Co., 170 Ky , 775, 187 S. W.
296 .
The circuit court has no authority to grant

for the recovery of money only where the amount
in controversy is less than $500 . Louisville &

775, 187 S. W. 296 .

human treatment . A decree of divorce granted

of appeals- but so much as awards , alimony may

§ 1307. Indictment for selling liquor to an
inebriate must allege that the defendant knew

Damron , 159 Ky . 444 ; 167 S. W. 381 .

makes no discrimination between the rich and
poor,and isconstitutional. Com .v. Sherley,11 R.
641; 12 S. W. 771.

offensesin which other than fineand imprisonment

frage. Eldridge v . Com ., 87 Ky . 365 ; 10 R. 176 ;

434;12 S.W. 256,thecourtheldthatthisstatute
was only applicable to offenses for which punish-
ment was provided by statute, but that case arose
before the enactment of the present statute; and
in Bottom v . Com ., 98 Ky . 17 ; 17 R. 555 ; 32 S. W.
140, the courtholdsthat thisstatuteappliesto
common law offenses, such as assault and battery ;
and see, further, as to construction of statute and
itsapplicabilityto cities. Bartlett v. City of Pad .,
28 R. 1174 ; 91 S. W. 264 .
This section applies to counties that have no
workhouse ; and a female may be required to work
in a workhouse erectedby a city. City v.Boyd , 19
R. 876 ; 42 S. W. 350 ; 101 Ky . 664 .
County attorney ; fees.- The county attorney
isnotentitledtocommissionon finesworkedoutunder this section. Powers v . Fleming County , 99

Instructions in the language of the statute are
sufficient. Smith v . Com ., 17 R. 416 ; 31 S. W. 471 ;
explainingtheopinioninEldridgev.Com.,87Ky .365 ; 10 R. 176 ; 8 S. W. 892 .
Judgment may include costs and prisoner may
be required to work out costs. Saylor v . Com ., 122
Ky . 755 ; 29 R. 337 ; 93 S. W. 12 .
Misfeasance or non -feasance in office . Failure
of jailerto require prisoner to work at hard labor
as directed by the judgment , is not such a mis
feasance as authorizes a forfeiture of his office.
The penalty is the fine imposed by the statute.
Lovell v . ('om ., 93 Ky . 507 ; 14 R. 496 ; 20 S. W.
540 .
Verdict must in terms provide for. It is not

guage of the statute is sufficient.

S. W. 811 .

set aside as to prior creditors a homestead was
set apart to him . The wife was a party to the
action. Her right in the property so set apartwas not affected as to subsequent creditors
by the setting of same apart as a homestead.
Beasley v . Gouge , 141 Ky . 34 , 132 S. W. 178.
An undivided interest in land descended to a
convict in the penitentiaryfrom his mother;
he intended to invest the proceeds of the sale
of same in a homestead ; his father's adminis-
trator sought to subject the son's interest in the
land to a debt . Eighteen months from the death
of his father at which time the life estate ter-
minated was a reasonable time to reinvest the
proceeds in a homestead . The proceeds were ex-
empt . Robinson v. Robinson, 142 Ky . 589, 134
S. W. 1130 .
A certain homestead was sold in the autumn
and a new homestead was purchased in the spring
and the deed was taken to the wife of the owner
of the first homestead . It was held that there
had been no abandonment of the homestead ; the
homestead was held exempt from a debt con-
tracted before the sale. Farmers ' and Traders '
Bank v . Childers, 150 Ky . 719, 150 S. W. 840.
A tract of land distant from the home place
about three hundred yards was included with it
as a homestead ; it had been used and cultivated
in connection with the home place. Farmer v.
Hampton , 154 Ky . 83, 156 S. W. 1041 .
On a motion for a writ of possession to a pur-
chaser at an executionsaleupon the evidence, it
was correctly decided by the circuit court that
the homestead had not been abandoned . Baker v .
Estridge,154Ky.659,157S.W. 1080.

doned her, and who has a right to asserthome-
stead in land occupied by him , which he has

the property in person or by agent, or tenant,
or otherwise, she willloseher right to the home-
stead. Purdy v. Melton, 164 Ky . 749, 176 S.W.
346 .

a homestead , abandons his wife and the homestead .
she may , for herself, assert and maintain her right
to the homestead. (Subsec. 4.) Purdy v. Melton,
164 Ky . 749 , 176 S. W. 346 .

conveyance by the husband to his wife . Mount v.
Fourth StreetBank , 156 Ky . 503, 161 8. W. 220.

not set up before the submission for judgment

quire the committee to recount the ballots. Henry

CHAPTER 43 .
(General Statutes, chapter 35.)
ESCAPES .
§ 1600. Warrant issued on affidavit; to
whom directed.- If any person rendered or
charged in custody, in execution or on
mesne process,or by any order of a judge
or chancellor,made inor out of court,shall
escape therefrom, or from the officerhav-
ing him in custody, any magistrate, upon
complaint and affidavitmade of the fact,
shall issue as many warrants for his re-
capture, directed to all sheriffsand con-
stables,and otherofficerswithinthisstate,
as he may deem necessary. The cause of
the person's commitment shall be men-
tioned in said warrant . Sheriffs, con-
stables and other like officersshall be also
commanded to recapturethe prisoner, and
forthwith to convey and commit him to the
prison of that county whence he escaped,
to be theresafelykept untildischargedby
due course of law . The warrant , with the
proper endorsement thereon, shallbe re-
turned by the proper officerto the clerk of
that court having jurisdictionof the cause
for which the prisoner was in custody.
§ 1601. Escape by one incustodyunder
finalprocess. If the prisoner was in cus-
tody by virtue of execution or finalprocess
when he escaped, he shall remain in close
jail, without bail or mainprize, untilhe
shallsatisfythe saiddemand , or untilthe
judgment or decree shall be reversed, or
he be discharged by due course of law .
§ 1602. Escape by one in custodyunder
mesne process.- If the prisoner was in cus-
tody by mesne processor other original
procedure, he shallremain in confinement,
afterhis capture, untilreleasedby due
course of law .
§ 1603. Prisonerin custody for crime
shallbe lodged in jail. If the prisoner was
in custody on a charge of treason, felony,
breach of the peace or misdemeanor , he
shall,upon being recaptured, be conveyed,
by the officerwho apprehends him , to the
jailof the county from which he escaped
and thereremain confineduntildischarged
by due course of law .
§ 1604. Officersliableon bond for negli-
gence ; verdict.- Officersand theirsureties
shallbe liable, in an action upon their offi-
cial bonds , for the use of the parties ag-
grieved, for the voluntary or negligent
escape of a prisoner in custody, for the
damages sustained. No judgment in such
action shallbe given, unless the jury shall,
by theirverdict, find " that the escape was
with the consent of the officer, or by his
negligence, or that such prisonermight
have been retakeniftheofficerhad,ingood
faith,made proper effortsto do so."
§ 1604. Capture or actual custody .- To make
an officerliable for an escape, the capture or ac-
tual custody of the prisoner by the officermust
be proved . Gordon v . Ryan , 1 J. J. M. 55 .
Consent or negligence of officer.- In an action
against an officerfor an escape, the jury must
find that the escape was with the consent or
throughthe negligenceof the officer. Noble v.
Beatty, 4 Bibb, 507; Biggs v. Rucker, 3 Litt.175.
Verdict that he suffered the prisoner " voluntarily
and negligently to escape ," held not sufficient.
Grimes v . Butler, 1 Bibb 192 .
Damages sustained. In an action on a jailer's
bond , for an escape, the plaintiffcan recover no
more damages than he can prove he has sustained ;
and if he does not prove that he lost the debt
or part of it in consequence of the escape, only
nominal damages can be recovered . Bernard v .
Com ., 4 Litt. 148 ; Johnson v . Lewis , 1 Dana 182 .
Force that may be used to prevent escape .-
An officerin making an arrest for felony, or in
retaking an escaped felon, may use such force as
is necessaryto capture the felon, even to killing
him when in flight. In a misdemeanor case the
rule is different. Head v. Martin, 85 Ky . 480; 9
R. 45 ; 3 S. W. 622 .
What is an escape . If a jailer lets a person
go out of the prison rules without giving bond ,
or upon giving a void bond , it is an escape. Com .
v. Gower , 4 Litt. 279 .
SEYMOUR'S NOTES
A judgment for nominal damages was proper
on the escape of an insolvent. Boyd v . Camp ,
10 Ky . Opinions 28 .
§ 1605. Penalty for aiding escape. If
any person shall aid a prisoner to escape,
or shall knowingly conceal him after he
escapes, or in any way hinder or prevent
hisrecapture,he shallbe liableto theparty
aggrievedforsuchdamages ashe may have
sustained .

§1606. Estates; escheat for failure of
heirsof persons to take.- That part of es-
tateslying or found in thiscommonwealth
notdisposedof by willof persons who have

or distributeesentitled to the same ,
which have been or may hereafterbe
devisedto any person who ,or any heir or
distributeeor devisee of his,or of the testa-
tor,has not claimed the same , or shallnot
claimthe same within eight years after
such death, shall vest in the common-
wealth subject to the debts and liabilities

§ 1606. Constitutionality of law relating to es-
cheats. The legislaturehas no power to authorize
a corporation or private citizen to sue for money
or property of one in the rightful possession, be-
cause it has no real owner , or upon the presump-
tion, by reason of the lapse of time, that no
owner exists, and to hold it as a gift from the
stateleaving the bailee responsibleto the real
owner, if he should appear, and requiringboth
to look to the donee of the state for its value .
Such legislation changes the legal status of the
parties without their consent . Louisville School
Board v. Bank of Kentucky , 86 Ky . 150; 9 R.
433; 5 S. W. 739 ; Bank of Louisville v . Board of
Trustees, 83 Ky . 219 ; 7 R. 185 ; see note to § 192,
constitution .
Escheater can only maintain action to recover
land that has vested in the state under this sec-
tion. Com . v . Wisconsin Chair Co., 119 Ky . 500;
27R. 170; 84 S. W. 535; Com .v.Farmers Bank,
27 R. 153 ; 84 S. W. 732 ; Com . v . Lou . Prop . Co.,
128 Ky . 790 ; 33 R. 227 ; 109 S. W. 1183 .
Lands escheated to the state are not embraced
in the general land law authorizing the appro-
priation of the vacant lands . Grants obtained
for such lands under the general laws are void .
Stith v. Hart , 6 Mon. 624; Jones v. Chiles, 4
J. J. M. 610 .
By escheatof land the stateacquires, as a pur-
chaser, all the rights of the former owner , as a
naturalperson, and if itbe granted the grantee
willhold it and be entitled to all the rights which
the first owner had . Grant by the state over-
reaches intervening grants or patents obtained
under the general law . Elmondorf v . Carmichael ,

smith, 85 Ky . 516; 9 R. 96; 4 S. W. 232.
When defendant surrenders land to be levied
on it is not necessary that officershould go upon
land or notify defendant that levy had been
made . Vallandingham v . Worthington , 85 Ky . 83 ;
8 R. 707; 2 S. W. 772 .
Where the levy states the number of acres, the
county where land lies, and the creek upon which
it is located and refers to the deeds for more
particular descriptions, it is sufficient. Bell v .
Weatherford , 12 Bush 505; Humphrey v. Wade ,
84 Ky . 391 ; 8 R. 384 ; 1 S. W. 648 ; Holcomb v .
Hays , 23 R. 352; 62 S. W. 1028; and the failure
of the officerto properly describeproperty will

324 ; 12 Bush 505 .
Land ; effect of levy upon .--A levy upon land
does not divest the debtor of either titleor pos-
session, nor does the officeracquire the possession
of iteitherin law or in fact,or become responsible
for itspreservation. Addison v . Crow ,5 Dana 271 ;
McBurnie v . Overstreet, 8 B. M. 300 .
The levyof an executioncreatesa mere lien,that is not completed until a sale and convey-
ance . Morton v . Robards , 4 Dana 258 ; and the
holder of an unrecorded mortgage upon property
levied on subsequent to the execution of the mort-
gage may , at any time before the sale under the
execution,by givingnoticeto the executioncredi-
tor, enforce his mortgage lien over the lien ac-
quired by the executionlevy. Baldwin v. Crow ,

331 ; 4 Dana 258 ; Bean v . Everett , 21 R. 1790 ;

As to prioritybetween executions, see notes
to § 1660 .
Land ; sales of under execution are not affected
by the reversal of the judgment under which

Execution for greater amount than judgment

Mistake as to number of acres in tract where

Sales have been held to be void only in cases

tion, or where officer exceeded his power and

Sale of land under an execution directed to

Sale of land, when debtor had sufficientper-
sonal property to satisfyexecution, is not void,

Personality; subject.--Money may be leviedon
if the officercan, without violence, get possession
of it; but the execution does not create a lien
before the levy. Doyle v. Sleeper, 1 Dana 531;
Stokes v. Coffey, 8 Bush 533; but money collected

the propertyof the plaintiffuntilpaid to him ,and
while it is in hands of sheriff can not be levied

First v . Miller, 4 Bibb 311 .
Choses in action are not subject to levy under

Ferran v. Jones, 2 Litt. 219.
Annual crops are personaltyand may be levied

205; Parham v . Thompson , 2 J. J. M. 159 ; but
not before October the first, unless severed from
the ground . See § 1696.
Property in possession of loanee for five years

Snoddy v.Foster, 1 Met .160; Withers v. Smith, 4
Bibb 170; Neal v.Elliott, 18 В. М. 604.
Personal property levied on under an attach-
ment or execution can not be levied on by another
officer. Oldham v. Scrivener, 3 B. M. 579; Rogers
v . Darnaby , 4 B. M. 238 .

an action of trespass but for the execution, and
he may take possession of the property or
leave it in possession of debtor or any other

Hill v.Harris,10 B. M. 120; but where the debtor
agrees to surrender certain property to satisfy

Debtor may dispose of his homestead by will,
and the devisee, if he resides on it with a family ,
will be entitled to homestead as against debts
created prior as well as subsequent to receiving
it. Pendergest v . Heekin , 94 Ky . 384 ; 15 R. 180 ;
22 S. W. 605 ; and see Nichols v . Lancaster , 17
R. 777 ; 32 S. W. 676.
Divorce ; subjection of homestead to alimony
and costs. Nunn v. Page , 134 Ky . 698; 121 S. W.
442 .
Exchange of lands . When land which one has
received in exchange for another tract is taken to
satisfy a lien for purchase money which existed
when he received land , he may recover the land
he gave , free from vendor's claim of homestead .
Williams v . Samuels , 90 Ky . 59 ; 11 R. 863 ; 13
S. W. 438. If land in which debtor is entitled
to a homestead is exchanged for other land, he
will be entitled to a homestead in it. Thompson
v . Heffner , 11 Bush 353 .
Fraudulent conveyance .- When a debtor , in con-
templation of insolvency, mortgages his property ,
he can not by moving on the land after suit has
been filedattacking the mortgage acquire a home-
stead as against his creditors. McCann v . Hill,
85 Ку . 574 ; 9 R. 137 ; 4 S. W. 337. But where a
debtor and his wife conveyed , in contemplation
ofinsolvency,theirhomesteadandotherproperty,
and the conveyance was held at the suit of credit-
ors to operate as an assignment under the act
of 1856 , the homestead exemption is not lost.
Davis v. Feltman , 112 Ky . 293 ; 23 R. 1510 ; 65
S. W. 615 ; Calloway v . Calloway ,19 R. 870 ; 39
S. W. 241; Allen v . Dillingham , 104 Ky . 801 ;
20 R. 980; 47 S. W. 1076. And it seems that if
the only property conveyed is the homestead ,worth
less than one thousand dollars, the homestead
will not be lostby such a conveyance. Lishy v.
Perry , 6 Bush 515 .
The homestead exemption is not lost by a
fraudulent conveyance (not assailed under act
of 1856 ) by husband and wife to a third party
who reconveys to wife of fraudulent grantor.
Kuevan v. Specker ,11 Bush 1 ; Dowd v . Hurley , 78
Ky . 260 ; Rothwell v . Rothwell , 31 R. 851 ; 104
S. W. 270 .
Gift . Homestead received as a gift is not
subject to debts created before it is so received.
Holcomb v . Hood , 12 R. 240 ; 1 S. W. 401 ; Hester
v . Lynn , 20 R. 1460 ; 49 S. W. 431 .
Homestead exemption ; who entitled to . It is
essential to the creation of the homestead that
the debtor should have a family , but not to the
continuance of the right, and the loss of family
by death or marriage does not deprive debtor of
homestead . Stultsv. Sale, 92 Ky . 5; 13 R. 337;
17 S. W. 148 ; Suter v . Quarles, 22 R. 1080 ; 58
S. W. 990 ; Gowdy v . Johnson , 104 Ky . 648 ; 20
R. 997 ; 47 S. W. 624 ; Holburn v . Pfaumiller , 114
Ky . 831 ; 24 R. 1613 ; 71 S. W. 940 ; Riddle v .
Fannin , 24 R. 1737 ; 72 S. W. 290 ; Rothwell v .
Rothwell , 31 R. 851 ; 104 S. W. 270 .
Debtor is entitled to homestead if he is a
housekeeper and has residingwith him any person
whom he is under a naturalor moral obligationto support. Bosquet v. Hall, 90 Ky . 566; 12 R.
433 ; 13 S. W. 244 ; Bell v . Keach , 80 Ky . 42 ; 3 R.
520 ; 11 Bush 622 ; and see Ellis v . Davis , 90 Ky .
183 ; 11 R. 893 ; 14 S. W. 74. But the fact that
a married daughter, who has not separated from
her husband, liveswith her father does not con-
stitutea family so as to exempt his homestead.
LouisvilleBk .Co. v.Anderson,21 R. 373; 44 S. W.
636 ; 106 Ky . 744 .
The right of exemption depends upon the present
and actual purpose and intentionof the debtor
to use and enjoy the property sought to be ex-
empted as a home for himself and family . Brown
v .Martin,4 Bush 47; Carter v.Goodman ,11 Bush
228 .
The debtor is not entitled to homestead in
property when both he and his family are per-
manently located elsewhere. Brown v. Martin, 4
Bush 47 .
A debtor is entitled to a homestead in land
upon which he residesat the time it is sought
to be subjected, though he may not have resided
on it when debt was created, provided the debt
was not created prior to the purchase of the land
or erectionof improvements. Hensey v. Hensey,92 Ky . 164; 13 R. 426; 17 S. W. 333; Morehead
v . Morehead , 16 R. 34; 25 S. W. 750; Holder v.Holder, 120 Ky . 802; 27 R. 1171; 87 S. W. 1100.
If the land was purchased or improvements
made priorto the creationof the debt, the home-
stead rightattacheswhen the debtor isoccupying
it as a homestead at the time it is attempted .

Donaldson v . Richart, 22 R. 1268; 60 S. W. 405;
Darnell v.Smith,98 Ky . 238; 17 R. 835; 32 S. W.
745 .
Sheriffs and their sureties are not entitled to
a homestead as against a judgment in favor ofthe commonwealth in an actionto recoverpublic
money . Com . v. Cook , 8 Bush 220; 12 Bush 283;Hutson v. Coombs , 23 R. 231; 62 S. W. 709.
Fines and costs.- A homestead exemption exists
as against executions for fines and costs. Com . v .
Lay , 12 Bush 283 .
Indivisibleproperty. Thompson v. Thompson ,
32 R. 319 ; 105 S. W. 1185 ; Warren v . Warren , 126
Ky . 692; 31 R. 1101; 104 S. W. 754.
Inherited land. Roberts v . Adams , 29 R. 848 ;
96 S. W. 554. See,further,casescitedin note (7).
Improvements .- Where a debtorplacesimprove-
ments on land and then occupies it for the first
time as a homestead , he will not be entitled to the
exemption as against debts created prior to the
erectionof the improvements. Fish v. Hunt , 81
Ky . 584; 5 R. 653; and see Nichols v. Sennitt, 78
Ky . 630; 5 R. 199; and 81 Ky . 554; 5 R. 636.
But only such buildingsor improvements as were
put upon property subsequent to the creationof
the debt can be subjectedwhen the property was
purchased and occupied before creationof debt.
Hemphill v. Haas , 88 Ky .492; 11 R. 62; 11 S. W.
510 ; Butler v. Davis , 15 R. 273 ; 23 S. W. 220 ; and
the debtor is entitled to a homestead exemption in
land to the extent of the value of improvements
placed on it before the creation of the debt . Dar-
nellv.Smith,98 Ky .238; 17 R. 835; 32 S. W. 745.
Intention to occupy .- Where there has never
been an occupancy of the land as a homestead ,
the mere intentionto so occupyit,consummated
by moving on it after it has been sold for debt ,
will not entitle the debtor to a homestead as
against the creditor. Fant v . Talbot , 81 Ky . 23 ;

Where husband and wife execute a mortgage ,
apparently regular, waiving their homestead , and
they are parties to an action to enforce it, and
make no defense, the judgment is a bar to a
subsequent action by them claiming homestead
on the ground that mortgage was not properly
acknowledged by wife . Honaker v . Cecil, 84 Ky .
202 ; 8 R. 188 ; 1 S. W. 392 ; and see Davis v .
Jenkins, 93 Ky . 353;353; 14 R. 342; 20 S. W. 283;
Harpending v. Wylie, 13 Bush 158; Derr v. Wil-
son , 84 Ky . 14 ; 7 R. 701 .
Failure to claim homestead in a suit to enforce
a mortgage upon it does not bar an action to
recover it, even after it has been sold under
judgment in the action to enforce mortgage, if
the deed did not pass the homestead . Wing v .
Hayden , 10 Bush 276; Hayden v. Robinson, 83
Ky . 615; 7 R. 707; McGrath v. Berry, 13 Bush
391 ; Crout v . Sauter , 13 Bush 442 ; and see 24
R. 2505 ; 74 S. W. 264.
Sale of homestead .- Owner of homestead has
a right to sell it without a valuable considera-
tion,as itisexempt from the claimsof creditors.
Tong v. Eifort, 80 Ky . 152; 3 R. 647; and the
husband may voluntarilysell and convey land
occupied as a homestead , although his wife does
not join in the deed , and when he does neither
husband nor wife can afterward claim homestead
in the land this sold. Brame v. Craig, 12 Bush
404 ; Pribble v. Hall, 13 Bush 61 ; Gillett v .
Arnett, 19 R. 1892; 44 S. W. 957; Rothwell v.
Rothwell, 31 R. 851; 104 S. W. 276; Paslick v.
Shay , 148 Ky . 642; 147 S. W. 369. As to effect
of fraudulent conveyance, see notes (11), (12).
Owner of homestead may sell it and invest
proceeds in another homestead; but if he con-
vertsitintomoneywithnopurposeofinvesting
in property exempt from execution, the proceeds
may be subjected by creditors. Lear v . Toten ,
14 Bush 101 ; and see Cooper v . Arnett , 95 Ky .
603 ; 16 R. 145 ; 26 S. W. 811 ; Tohermes v. Beiser,
93 Ky . 415 ; 14 R. 440 ; 20 S. W. 379 ; Welch v .
Spraggins, 98 Ky . 279; 17 R. 884; 32 S. W. 943.
Title bond .- Widow is entitled to a homestead
in land held by her husband under a title bond .
Persifull v . Hind , 88 Ky . 296 ; 10 R. 880 ; and
the husband may have homestead in land held
undera contract of purchase . The legal title
is not necessary to create the right to homestead .
Griffin v . Proctor , 14 Bush 571 ; Carr v. Winlock ,
109 Ky . 488 ; 22 R. 1047 ; 59 S. W. 747 .
Two tracts.- A debtor owned two adjoining
tracts of land , both of which he cultivated; the
one on which he resided he sold, but continued
to resideon it after the sale, and while he re-
sided upon it the other tract was sold under an
execution against him . Having erected a houseon the tract sold under execution , after the
execution sale, and moved on the tract, he is
entitledto homestead as against execution pur-
chaser . Bennett v . Baird , 81 Ky . 554 ; 5 R. 636 ;
and see Fish v. Hunt , 81 Ky . 584; 5 R. 653;
Mason v . Columbia F. & T. Co., 99 Ky . 117 ;
18 R. 40 ; 35 S. W. 115 ; Redmon v . Citizens Bank ,
19 R. 137; 39 S. W. 432; Donaldson v. Richart,
22 R. 1268; 60 S. W. 405; Green v . Pennington,
30 R. 203 ; 97 S. W. 766 ; Gaar Scott Co. v . Reesor ,
28 R. 1308; 91 S. W. 717; Holder v. Holder,
120 Ky . 802 ; 27 R. 1171 ; 87 S. W. 1100 ; Frazier
v . Potter , 150 Ky . 127 ; 150 S. W. 19 .The debtor is entitled to a homestead in two
adjoining tracts, upon one of which he resides,
when the value of both of them does not exceed
one thousand dollars, and the fact that he had
given a mortgage on the tract containing resi-
dence does not affect the question. Franks v .
Lucas, 14 Bush 395. And see Slaughter v. Karn ,
15 R. 429 ; 23 S. W. 791. Buckler v . Brown , 19
R. 85 ; 39 S. W. 429 ; 101 Ky . 46 .
A debtor owning two tracts of land , who
executes a mortgage upon one and occupies the
other as a homestead , thereby elects to claim
as his homestead the tract not mortgaged , and
he can not assert claim to homestead in the
other tract; though the mortgage did not convey
homestead exemption therein. Hayden v . Robin-
son, 83 Ky . 615 ; 7 R. 707 .
When a debtor mortgages the land upon which
his home is situated, and it is sold to satisfy
the mortgage debt , he can not claim homestead in
other lands owned by him . Jarboe v . Colvin,
4 Bush 70 .
The owner of two adjoining city lots, who
has resided many years upon one of them as
his homestead, it being worth over one thousand
dollars, can not prevent his creditors from sub-
jecting the other lot by moving upon it. Toher-
mes v. Beiser, 93 Ky . 415; 14 R. 440; 20 S. W.
379; Garrison v. Penn , 23 R. 1775; 66 S. W. 14.
Warranty ; breach of.--Homestead of war-
rantor may be subjected to claim for damages
on account of, although actionwas not instituted
until after land was purchased . Benge v . Bowl-
ing, 106 Ky . 574; 21 R. 165; 51 S. W. 151.
Wife can not during life of husband assert
claim to homestead unless he has abandoned her
or fails to assert his right thereto. Frazier v .
Brashears,Brashears, 23 R. 2232; 66 S. W. 1038; Daisy v.
Houlihan,19 R. 1337; 43 S. W. 487; Hemphill
v. Haas , 88 Ky . 492; 11.R. 62; 11 S. W. 510;
but is entitled to claim homestead in her own
land as against her debts. Herring v. Johnson,
24 R. 1940 ; 72 S. W. 793 .

Homestead existed in land not occupied by

set aside; practice; when lien not affected.
-Sales made under execution by fraud.
covin or collusion may be set aside on the
motion of any personaggrieved,or by pe-
tition in equity .
1. If by motion , it must be commenced

the execution issued .

§ 1711. See note (32 ) to $ 1692 .

§1956.Recoveryof money lostat gaming.-
Where there is lost at a wager as much as five
dollars at one time , the right of the loser to re-
cover it from the winner exists, and he may sue
therefor, or for the aggregate amount so lost dur-
ing a given period without regard to when the bet
was made , or how long it was pending and un-
determined. Lyons v. Hodgen , 90 Ky . 280; 12 R.
211; 13 S. W. 1076. See, further, as to recovery
of money , Roberts v. Respass, 131 Ky . 631; 114
S. W. 341; Cartwright v. McElwain , 132 Ky . 83;
116 S. W. 297; Holzbog v. Bakrow , 156 Ky . 161;
160 S. W. 792 .
The proprietorof a gaming house who receives
a certain per cent, of the winnings of each game
called the " take out," is a " winner " in the
meaning of thissection,and the losermay recover
from him what he has lost. Triplettv. Seelbach,
91 Ky . 30 ; 12 R. 661 ; 14 S. W. 948 ; and see Stapp
v. Mason , 114 Ky . 900; 24 R. 1680; 72 S. W. 11;
and notes to § 1955 .
Where money is lost at gaming any creditor
of the loser, who chooses to assert his right to
recover it, may do so. Caldwell v. Caldwell, 2
Bush 446 .
A wife, pending her suitfor alimony and di-
vorce, may to the extentof the alimony adjudged
to her , recover from persons the money won from
her husband betting on a horse race. Cain v .
McHarry , 2 Bush 263 .
Persons who engage in gaming by means of
sellingpools on horse races can not recover from
the winner under this section; where one seeks
to recover of pool-sellers money they have won
from him , they are entitled to deduct from the
amount he claims the sums which he has won
from them . Elias v . Gill, 92 Ky . 569 ; 13 R. 798 ;

857 § 1910FRAUDULENT AND PREFERENTIAL CONVEYANCE .
with the design to prefer. Heidrich v. Silva, 89
Ky . 422 ; 11 R. 645 ; 12 S. W. 770 .
Preference is not void , but only voidable at
the election of creditorswho sue within six months ,
and unless the preference is assailed in the man-
ner pointed out in the statute and within six
months , it will not be disturbed . Whitehead v .
Woodruff,11 Bush 209;German Bank v.Jefferson,
10 Bush 326 .
Preferred creditors; refunding by .-Money paid
to preferred creditors must be refunded . Baker
v . Kinnaird, 94 Ky . 5; 14 R. 695; 21 S. W. 237.
Prior agreement ; mortgage in pursuance of,
executed by an insolvent debtor , will operate as
an assignment . McCutcheon v . Caldwell , 90 Ky .
249 ; 12 R. 145 ; 13 S. W. 1072 ; Darnell v . Lewis ,
94 Ky . 455 ; 15 R. 222 ; 22 S. W. 843 ; but where
commission merchants advance money under a
written agreement that tobacco shall be purchased
with money and shipped to them and the tobacco
is reduced to possessionbefore creditorsassail
transaction as a preference it is not within the
statute. Brooks v . Staton , 79 Ky . 174 ; 2 R. 56 ;
and see Hoffman v . Brungs , 83 Ky . 400 ; but such
transactionwill be a preferenceif property has
not been reduced to possessionby person furnish-
ing money before other equities intervene . Cook
v. Brannin ; 87 Ky . 101; 9 R. 955; 7 S. W. 877;
see, further, Corn v . Sims , 3 Met . 391 ; Elliott
v . Harris , 9 Bush 237 .
Recording of mortgage . A mortgage executed
by an insolvent debtor to secure a debt simul-
taneously created may be assailed under this sec-
tion unless it is recorded in thirty days from
its execution. Farmer v . Hawkins , 79 Ky . 182 ;
3 R. 92. For a full discussion of the meaning of
the last clause of this section, see Meier v . Flins-
bach, 95 Ky . 139 ; 15 R. 482 ; 24 S. W. 235 ,
Renewal of lien , executed to secure a debt
simultaneouslycreated, does not bring the re-
newal within the operation of the statute. O'Neil
v . Miller , 2 Bush 289 ; Drake v . Ellman , 80 Ky .
434 ; 4 R. 269 .
Simultaneous and pre -existing debt .- Where a
mortgage is executed by an insolvent debtor to
secure a debt created simultaneouslywith. its
execution and a pre -existing debt , it will be valid
as to the former , but within the statute as to the
latter . McCutcheon v . Caldwell , 90 Ky . 249 ; 12 R.
145 ; 13 S. W. 1072 ; Farmer v . Hawkins , 79 Ку .
182 ; 3 R. 92 ; Whittaker v . Garnett , 3 Bush 402 ;
Southworth v . Casey , 78 Ky . 395 ; Slusher v . Simp-
kinson , 19 R. 1184 ; 40 S. W. 570 ; 43 S. W. 692 ; 101
Ky . 594 ; but if such creditor knows that the
debtor is insolvent, and aids the arrangement, he
will not be protected, even to the extent of the
debt simultaneously created. McCann v . Hill, 85
Ky . 574 ; 9 R. 137 ; 4 S. W. 337 .
Surety who , subsequent to becoming bound ,
takes a mortgage for his indemnity from his prin-
cipal is within the statute. McCann v. Hill, 85
Ky . 574 ; 9 R. 137 ; 4 S. W. 337.
Voluntary assignment .- A creditor can not
maintain an action to have an assignment made
by his debtor set aside on the ground that the
debtor , beforemaking assignment, made a prefer-
ential conveyance , if the assignee has assailed the
preferential conveyance. Hall v. Rothchild, 19
R. 1621; 44 S. W. 108; 102 Ky . 582.
Suit must be brought within six months . Tur-
ner v .Farmers Bank ,148 Ky . 692; 147 S. W. 435.
Property in other state ; how affected . Fawcett
v . Mitchell , 133 Ky . 361 ; 117 S. W. 956 .

One seeking to have a mortgage declared prefer-
ential, should set forth all the necessary aver-
ments , and a denial of knowledge of the informa-
tion as to whether the mortgagee loaned the
mortgagorthe money, which the mortgage pur-ported to secure, simultaneouslywith the mort-
gage or at any time, is not sufficient. Kelly v .
Yandell , 18 R. 462 , 36 S. W. 1127 ; Borches v .
Williams,19 R. 1532, 43 S. W. 683.
The assignees had no lien on the property
conveyedby W. to securea repaymentof themoney advanced as the deed of assignment had
not the effect of a mortgage executed to secure
a debt created simultaneously therewith . Louis-
villeTrust Co. v . Columbia Finance & T. Co.,22 R.
1086 , 59 S. W. 867 .
The fact that when an insolvent made a con-
veyance of real estate' and when he subsequently
made an assignment for the benefitof creditors
the national bankruptcy act was in force, did
not preclude the assignee from suing to bring
the propertyconveyed intothe trustfund. Downer
v. Porter, 116 Ky . 422, 25 R. 571, 76 S. W. 135.
A mortgage executed in good faith for a debt
created simultaneously and not recorded within
thirtydays is not a preferencewithin this sec-
tion. Union Trust & Savings Co. of Maysville
v. Taylor, Ky . 129 S. W. 828; Taylor v . Deposit
Bank of Pearce, Fant & Co., Ky . 129 S. W. 828.
A payment of money in the ordinary course
of business with no intent to prefer is not a
preference within this section. Union Trust &
Savings Co. of Maysville v. Taylor, Ky . 129 S. W.
828; Taylor v. Deposit Bank of Pearce, Fant &
Co., Ky . 129 S. W. 828.
One having a right to purchase land at a cer-
tain price exercisedthe option, and caused the
land to be conveyed to a bank , which advanced
part of the purchase money and held the title
as security, but did not record the deed. This
was not a preferencewithin this section. Union
Trust & Savings Co. of Maysville v. Taylor, Ky .
129 S. W. 828; Taylor v.Deposit Bank of Pearce,
Fant & Co., Ky . 129 S. W. 828.
A transfer to a creditor by one who believed
himself solvent and who should have known that
he was insolvent, is presumed to be a preference
within this section. Union Trust & Savings Co.
of Maysville v . Taylor , Ky . 129 S. W. 828 ; Taylor
v . Deposit Bank of Pearce , Fant & Co., Ky . 129
S. W. 828 .
(Modifying paragraphs 7 and 8, §1910.)
A mortgage was made to a trust company which
furnished money with which certain debts were
paid preferringthese creditorsin contemplation
of insolvency. This transaction was within this
section. Union Trust & Savings Co. of Mays-
ville, Ky . v. Taylor, 142 Ky . 183, 134 S. W. 196.
An unrecorded mortgage not within this sec-
tion secured a debt ; out of money borrowed on
a subsequent mortgage this debt and other debts
were paid ; the subsequent mortgage was not
invalid as to this debt although within the statute
as to the other debts . Union Trust & Sav . Co.
of Maysville, Ky ., v. Taylor, 142 Ky . 183, 134 S.
W. 196 .
A certain payment by an involved debtor was
held not to be within the statute . Cecil v . Cit .
Nat . Bank , 145 Ky . 842, 141 S. W. 416.

By a written unrecorded lease a husband be- | held fraudulentas to a debt of the husband. Perry
came the tenant of his wife and her mother as to
certain land . He surrendered to the wife certain
tobacco raised on the land ; she sent it to a ware-
house company ; and it was sold within 120 days
after the rent became due . The surrender of the
tobacco was not in writing nor was it recorded.
This surrender was invalid as to creditors of the
husband ; but the wife's lien as landlord for rent
owing to her remained in force as to the tobacco.
Jones v . Louisville Tob . W. H. Co., 121 S. W. 633 .
If the husband and wife join in an agreement
to exchange the homestead , such agreement is
enforceable against both. Jones v. Jones, 127
S. W. 795 .
A married woman may sue the firm of which
her husband is a member for money lent to it
before 1894. Parker, Jones & Steelv.Parker, 25
R. 2193 ; 80 S. W. 209 .
A married woman can not become personally
liable as surety for anyone . Baker v . Owensboro
Savings Bank & Trust Co.'sReceiver,140 Ky .121;
130 S. W. 969 .
A deed to land not containing words of con-
veyance was held to correctand make good a
former deed of a married woman which was void
because her husband was no party to the same .
East JellicoCoal Co. v. Jones, 141 Ky . 306; 132
S. W. 411 .
A husband may make a gift of personalprop-
erty to his wife orally; such giftwill be binding
on him , his heirs, and distributees. McWethy's
Admx . v. McCright, 141 Ky . 816; 133 S. W. 1001.
A wife may become indebted to her husband or
the husband to her ; the indebtedness may be sued
on as in case of any other debtor. Coleman v.
Coleman, 142 Ky . 36; 133 S. W. 1003.
A deed of a married woman to land in which
her husband does not join passesno title. Simp-
son v. Smith, 142 Ky . 608; 134 S. W. 1166.
A propertycontractenteredintobetween a hus-
band and wife after they had separated was
upheld. Luttener v. Luttener, 143 Ky . 844; 137
S. W. 777 .
A widow paid out of her own means demands
due by the estateof her husband. She was entitled
to assert a demand against his estate for the
amount so paid. Gilliam v. Gilliam, 146 Ky . 15;
141 S. W. 370 .
A woman who marriedbefore1893had a rightto sue without her husband on a claim which had
not been reduced to his possession. Walker v.
Milliken, 150 Ky . 12; 150 S. W. 71.
An actionwas brought by a divorced husband
seeking to modify the judgment awarding to his
wife the custody of the child. The wife had mar-ried again; so had the husband. Upon the evi-
dence the court refused to disturbthe judgment.
Colson v. Colson, 153 Ky .68; 154 S. W. 380.
An unrecorded mortgage executed by a married
woman and her husband is valid between the par-
ties. Woods v. Davis, 153 Ky . 99; 154 S. W. 905.
A married woman being under disabilitymade
a contract to devise. After the enactment of this
statute, which removes the disabilityof married
women , she reiterated and confirmed the same

was valid. Skinner v. Raske , 165 Ky . 108; 176
S. W. 942 .
A certain deed from a husband to his wife was

was executed before 1893 , provides that she shall
have no power to mortgage or encumber same .
Monroe v. Monroe , 155 Ky . 112; 159 S. W. 651.
