§2136 as gives the wife an absolute right to relin-
quish a conveyance or deviseby way of jointure
made after her marriage . Redwine's Ex . v . Red-
wine , 160 Ky . 282 ; 169 S. W. 864 .
A married woman has a right to sue for pos
session of her land without joining her husband .
Limitationbegins to run againsther from the time

extends until three years after she becomes dis-
covert. Big Sandy Co. v. Ramey , 162 Ky . 236;
172 S. W. 508 .

by which propertywas to be conveyed to the wife.

take effect. Marvel v. Marvel, 163 Ky . 601; 174

Under this section and §§ 2506 and 2510 , a right
of action by a married woman to recover land

Ramey ,162 Ky . 236; 172 S. W. 508.
Under an allegation of a transfer from husband
to wife without showing whether the transferwas

This sectionand §1706,relatingto mortgage of

rate use of the daughter, free from the control

strued independentlyof the statute, and if she

This sectionand $ 2127 relatingto the right
of husband in the wife's property are not retro-
spectiveand do not affectthe rightsof the hus-
band under the law as it existed prior to the
enactment of these sections. Tucker v . Tucker's
Admr ., 165 Ky . 306; 176 S. W. 1173.

1019 § 2132HUSBAND AND WIFE
in land held as partnershipstock. The wife of a
deceasedpartnerhasno interestuntilthepartner-
ship debts are paid. Galbreath v.Gedge ,16 B. M.
635 ; Pepper v . Thomas , 85 Ky . 539 ; 9 R. 122 ; 4
S. W. 297 .
Presumption of husband'sdeath by absence
from the stateseven years,without any proof that
he was alive within that time , entitleshis wife to
dower in land conveyed by the husband. Foulks
v .Rhea ,7 Bush 568 .
Remainder. The widow isnotentitledtodower
in land in which her husband, at the time of his
death, owned only a vested interestin remainder.
Carter v. McDaniel , 94 Ky . 565; 15 R. 349; 23
S. W. 507 .
Right of widow to clear land .- Doweress of un-
cleared land has the right to clear it, so far as
her full enjoyment of her estate as a home may
require; and to that extent may remove the tim-
ber and appropriate it to the expenses of her neces-
sary improvements. Fritzv.Tudor,1 Bush 28.
Sale of infant husband's land for reinvestment .
-If an infant husband's land be sold under decree
for reinvestment in other land , and he dies after
the sale, but before reinvestment , his widow will
only take one-third of the money for life. Collins
v . Champ ,15 В. М. 118 .
Sale of whole estate because indivisible .- A
widow having only a dower right can not procure
a sale of the whole property upon the ground that
her dower can not be assigned without materially
impairing the value of the whole estate. Lieder-
kranz Society v. Beck , 8 Bush 597 ; see also Rich
v . Rich , 7 Bush 53 .
Sale subjectto dower.- Although therewas no
directionin the judgment to sellthe land, subject
to the wife's contingentrightof dower, the com-
missionershould so sellit. Robinson v.Robinson,
11 Bush 174 .
Purchaser subjectto contingentright of dower
will not be permitted to deny the existenceof the
dower right. Pepper v. Thomas ,85 Ky . 539; 9 R.
122 ; 4 S. W. 297 .
Sale under judgment in favor of state.- Wife's
dower was not lost or transferred by the sale of
the land to satisfy a judgment against the husband
as surety on a sheriff'sbond for the collectionof
Vinson v . Gentry , 14 R. 804 ; 21 S. W.revenue .
578 .
Seizin of husband .- Present statute makes no
change . Smallridge v. Hazlett, 112 Ky . 841; 66
S. W. 1043; 23 R. 2228. A widow is not entitled
to dower in land unlessher husband, while they
were married , was beneficiallyseized of it. Fon-
taine v . Dunlap , 82 Ky . 321; 6 R. 201; Gully v .
Ray ,18 B. M. 107. Widow is not entitled to dower
in land which the husband had , before the mar
riage , sold by executory contract, either verbal or
written,althoughhe did not convey the legaltitle
to the purchaser until after he was married ; 18 В.
M. 107 ; Oldham v . Sale, 1 B. M. 76 ; Dean v .
Mitchell, 4 J.J. M. 451. There must be an actual
seizin, or a rightto an actualseizin, by the hus-
band during coverture to entitlehis widow to
dower . Testatordevised land to his son, subject
to his mother's life estate . The son's estate was
disposedofduringhiscoverture. He died,leaving
a widow , and his mother also survivinghim . His
widow was not entitled to dower . Butler v . Cheat-
ham , 8 Bush 594; Cate v. Ganter, 31 R. 892; 104
S. W. 296. The true testof the rightof dower is,
that the issueof thewifeby the marriagemight
inherit the estate from the husband as his heir.
Id. A widow is entitledto dower, as legateeby
implication, inthelifeestatewhichwas devisedto her husband, with remainderat his death topass by the law of descent to his descendants.
Jacob v. Jacob,4 Bush 110; 11 Bush 646. A pur-
chaseris not estopped, by the husband'sdeed,from showing the nature of his seizin,and that itwas not such as secureddower to hiswidow . Gully
v.Ray ,18 B. M. 107. When a fatherin a convey-ance stipulatedthathisson'swife shouldnot have
dower in the land, if she survived him, the wifesurvivingis not entitledto dower. Thompson v .
Vance,1 Met.669. See furtherFergusonv.Fer-
guson, 153 Ky .742; 156 S. W. 413.
Trust estate.- Widow is entitled to dower where
the husband has an estate of inheritance in the
use of trust. Herron v.Williamson,Litt.Sel.Cas.
251; Bailey v. Duncan , 4 Mon. 256. The wife of
a trustee has no dower in a trust estate, but the
wife of the cestuique trusthas. Stevens v. Smith,
4 J.J. M. 64;Bartlettv.Gouge ,5 B. M. 152. The
statuteembraces no impliedtrusts,except such asthe husband holds at the time of his death . Hamil-
ton v.Hughes ,6 J.J.M. 581.Value of dower in land alienated by husband .--
Widow is entitledto the use of one-third, esti-
mated according to quantity, quality and value,
when allotted, except so far as the purchaserhasincreasedthevalueby improvements.ents. Fritzv.
Tudor,1 Bush 28; Vinson v.Gentry, 14 R. 804; 21
S.W. 578; Lawson v .Morton , 6 Dana 471; Pepper
v.Thomas,85 Ky .539; 9 R. 122; 4 S.W. 297.
Widow renouncing will.- A widow who re-
nounces her husband's will has no right to have
land directedby the willto be sold, and the pro-ceedsdistributedto devisees,treatedas personalty,and have distribution. Her interest can not be
increasedor diminished by the will. Barnett v .Barnett, 1 Met . 254. Where a husband conveyed
property to a trustee, for his wife, in order tosecureher a home , and then made a willand died,
the widow upon renouncing the willis entitledto
dower . Worsley v . Worsley , 16 B. M. 455. Where
the husband made his will before marriage, the
widow need not renounce it,as she is not affected
by it. Loughborough v. Loughborough , 14 B. M.
553 .
Widow taking under will.- If a widow takes
under the will, she holdsas deviseemerely; but if
the estatebe settledon her before marriage as a
jointurein lieuof dower, or if she renounces the
will and has dower allotted,her estateis not sub-
ject to the debts of her husband . Chambers v.
Davis, 15 B. M. 522. Where the will gives the
widow an estateduringlifeor widowhood ,without
any deviseover, her subsequentmarriage,without
renouncingthe will, terminatesher interestin the
estate. Smith v.Bone ,7 Bush 367. Where testator
directs that his debts be paid , and then devises to
his wife one-third of his land , she failing to re-
nounce the will, takes the land as devisee, and
must contribute to the payment of testator'sdebt .
Hinson v . Ennis, 81 Ky . 363; 5 R. 367; and see,
further, notes (8) and (9), § 1702.

1043 § 2219INTEREST AND USURY
Payments on judgment ; right of action.- No
right to recoverusury paid on a judgment accrues
to the debtor as long as the judgment is in force.
The statute of limitation does not begin to run
againsta suitto recoverusury paid on a judg-
ment until the judgment is annulled . Kendall v .
Crouch , 88 Ky . 199; 10 R. 993; 11 S. W. 587.
Premium in excess of legal interest paid as an
inducement for a loan is usury . Gordon v . Win-
chesterBldg .Assn .,12 Bush 110; Herbert v.Ken-
ton Bldg .Assn ., 11 Bush 296 .
Presumption arising from credits. Though the
note, by its terms, bears eight per cent interest,
it will not be presumed, from the mere giving of
a creditof intereston it, that the payment was
made at that rate. Hicks v. Shouse,17 B. M. 483.
Release of claim to usury by debtor to creditor,
or agreement that he willnot claim the usury he
promised to pay, isvoid. Browning v. Thompson ,
13 В. М. 387 .
Remedy at law or in equity. A borrower may ,
by an action at law , recover usury paid by him
eitherupon a judgment at law or in equity. Sher-
ley v . Trabue , 85 Ky . 71 ; 8 R. 649 ; 2 S. W. 656 .
For old rule see Moss v . Rowland , 1 Duv . 321 ;
Scott v.Shropshire, 2 Duv .153; Chinn v. Mitchell,
2 Met . 92 ; Ross v . Ross , 3 Met . 274 ; Pearce v .
Hedrick , 3 Litt. 109 ; Thompson v . Ware , 8 B. M.
26 ; Moran v . Woodyard , Id ., 537. In any case
where it is plain from the recordthat a party is
seeking to recover usury, the chancellorshould
refuse to give judgment for the usury, although
the plea is not made by the defendant. Hill v.
Cornwall , 95 Ky . 512 ; 16 R. 97 ; 26 S. W. 540 .
Renewal of note.- A note given in renewal of
one which containedusury iswithout consideration
to the extent of the usury embraced therein. The
renewal of a note tainted with usury is not a
payment of the usury, and limitationas to itdoes
not then begin to run . Rudd v . Planters ' Bank ,
78 Ky . 513; Fitzpatrickv. Apperson, 79 Ky . 272;
2 R. 249. See as to effect of national banking
law , Brown v . Marion National Bank , 92 Ky . 607 ;
13 R. 812 ; 18 S. W. 635 ; and note (14 ). Where ,
in the renewal of a note, there is a change of
payee, or of a part of the obligors, those bound
upon the old obligationwillbe dischargedbecause
there is a new contract; but such a novation isnot a payment of usury, and if usury be carried
intothe new noteitwill,upon plea,be extracted,any payments theretoforemade being treated, at
the electionof the debtor, as paid upon principal
and legal interest. Kendall v . Crouch, 88 Ky.199; 10 R. 993; 11 S. W. 587; Hillv. Cornwall, 95
Ky . 512; 16 R. 97; 26 S. W. 540; Neal v. Rouse,93 Ky . 151; 14 R. 126; 19 S. W. 171; Shirleyv .
Stephenson,104 Ky .518; 20 R. 767; 47 S. W. 581;Mann v.Bank ,104Ky .852; 20 R. 1033; 48 S.W.413. These cases, in effect, overrule Smith v.
Young , 11 Bush 393. If a residuarydeviseere-
ceives notesof the executorcontainingusury, and
gives them up and takesnew notes, the obligordoes not losehisrightto have the usury purgedfrom the new note. Smith v. Broyles, 15 B. M.
461 .
Renewal of note to assignee. If the obligorgivesa new notetotheassigneeforthedebt,in-cludingthe usury, hisrightto have a deductionis gone,but he may recover itback from the as-
signor. Breckenridgev.Churchill,3 J.J.M. 11;Stone v.McConnell,1 Duv .54; see Clark v.Rodes ,
12 Bush 13; and see, further,Kendallv. Crouch,
88 Ky . 199; 10 R. 998; 11 S. W. 587.
Rent , after it is due , shall carry interest like
other liabilities. Moore v . Calvert, 6 Bush , 356 .
See § 2299 .
Right to recover usury is assignable, and as-
signoris not a necessaryparty. FidelityTrust
Co. v.Ryan , 22 R. 734; 58 S. W. 610.
Taxes; intereston. Com .v. L. & N. R. Co., 31
R. 819 ; 104 S. W. 267 .
When obligation begins to bear interest.- Where
note or obligationissilentas to when interestis

from the time it falls due or becomes payable .
Carr v . Robinson , 8 Bush 270. But where a note
was payable in two years with interestfrom
until paid it bore interest from its date .
Miller v . Cavanaugh , 99 Ky . 377 ; 18 R. 183 ; 35
S. W. 920 .

CHAPTER 72a '
INVESTMENT COMPANIES *
The act of March 22 , 1902 , с. 82 , p . 184 , here
compiled , was originally section 2223a of the 1903 and
1909 editions of the Kentucky Statutes. In the 1915
edition the insertion of an act concerning " interpreters"
for certain courts required the change of the act here
compiled to section 2223b . However , the act which was
section 2223a in the 1915 edition was originally sections
1045-1049 , inclusive, of the 1894 and 1899 editions, be-
ing superseded by an act of 1902 compiled as section 1038a
of the 1903 and 1909 editions, which section 1038a of
said editions comprised the law given in section 2223a
of the 1915 edition. Said law relating to " interpreters"
will now be found in this and all future editions as
sections 1019c -1, et seq. Many good reasons would
seem to require that the law compiled in the 1903 and
1909 editions as section 2223a should continue to bear
this section number in this and all future editions, and
it is therefore re-compiled accordingly.- [Ed .)

§ 2514. Accrual of cause of action upon con-
tracts. The statutebeginsto run only from theaccrualof the cause of action, not from the date
of the promise. Banks v. Coyle, 2 Mar. 564. If a
suretypays the note and takes an assignment, his
action is then upon the note , but the law does not
per se make the assignment , and if he waits more
than five years before having the assignment
made his right is lost. He might eithervolun-
tarily or coercivelyobtain the assignment at
any time before the five years ' bar . Joyce v .
Joyce , 1 Bush 474. A cause of action on an ad-
ministrator's bond accrues to the distributee nine
months after the qualificationof the administrator .
Robinson v . Elam , 90 Ky . 300 ;12 R. 271 ; 14 S.
W. 84 .
Action against heir on note of ancestor . The
limitationof fifteenyears applies. TrusteesKy .
F. O. S. v. Fleming , 10 Bush 234.
Action to enforce lien.- If a note is barred ,
the lien; whether a vendor's lien or a mortgage ,
by which it is secured ,can not be enforced . Yeates
v. Weeden , 6 Bush 438; Prewitt v. Wortham , 79
Ky . 287 ; 2 R. 282 ; Kendall v . Clark , 90 Ky . 179 ;
11 R. 980 ; 13 S. W. 583 ; Hamilton v . Wright , 27
R. 1144 ; 87 S. W. 1093 ; Clift v . Williams , 105
Ky . 559 ; 20 R. 1261 ; 49 S. W. 328. Where the
land has been conveyed to a remote vendee , and
the originalpurchaserhas by partialpayments on
his purchase notes extended the statute, such ex-
tension can not affect the lien as against the re-
mote vendee . Tate v . Hawkins , 81 Ky . 577 ; 5 R.
626; but if stranger buys land or a mortgage is
taken upon it before the expiration of fifteen
years,the lifeof the vendors lienmay be extended
by partial payment's on notes. Cook v . Union
Trust Co., 106 Ky . 803 ; 21 R. 454 ; 51 S. W. 600 .
Bond of guardian .-The lapse of fifteen years
after the marriage of the female ward bars an
action by the husband , or the husband and wife ,
against the guardian on his bond . Finnell v .
O'Neal , 13 Bush 176.
Bond of personal representative.- Action upon
administrator's bond is barred after fifteen years
from the time the cause of action firstaccrued ,
as to the principal, and in fiveyears as to the
surety. After the action upon the bond is barred ,
there can be no liabilityby reason of the implied
undertaking. Hargis v. Sewell, 87 Ky . 63; 9 R.
920 ; 7 S. W. 557. The cause of action upon the
bond accrues to the distributee nine months after
the qualification of the administrator . Robinson
v . Elam , 90 Ky . 300 ; 12 R. 271 ; 14 S. W. 84.
Breach of covenant of warranty .- An action
to recover damages for a breach of warranty of
titleto land is not barred until fifteenyears after
the cause of action accrued . Thomas v . Bland , 91
Ky . 1 ; 12 R. 640 ; 14 S. W. 955 .
Contract in writing .- Acceptance of deed and
possession of land by grantee operate as an agree-
ment by him to pay the purchase price recited
in the deed, and an action thereforis permitted
upon a contractin writing. Elliottv. Saufley, 89
Ky . 52; 10 R. 958; 11 S. W. 200. See as to a
mortgage tosecurean account,Prewittv .Wortham ,
79 Ky . 287 ; 2 R. 282 .
A due billis a written obligationfor the pay-
ment of money ,and an actionthereonis not barred
until after the lapse of fifteen years . White v .
Curd , 86 Ky . 191 ; 9 R. 505 ; 5 S. W. 553 .
Contracts in violation of statute are void . Union
Central Co. v. Spinks, 119 Ky . 261; 26 R. 1205;
83 S. W. 615 .
Dividends .- Action by stockholder to recover
accrues when dividends has been declared, but
the fifteen-year statuteof limitationapplies. W. &
L. T. P. Co. v. Wickliffe, 100 Ky . 531; 18 R. 964;
38 S. W. 866 .
Judgments ; domestic.- Lapse of fifteen years,
without issuingexecution, bars any further pro-
ceedings on the judgment ; and if another execu-
tion is issued it will be quashed on motion . Lock-
heart v. Yeiser, 2 Bush 231; McArthur v . Goddin ,
12 Bush 274; Proctor v. Bell, 97 Ky . 98 ; 16 R.
823; 30 S. W. 15; White v. Moore , 18 R. 790; 38
S. W. 505 ; 100 Ky . 358 ; and see Swafford v .
Howard,20 R. 1793; 50 S.W. 43; and see McDon-ald v. Stembridge, 116 Ky . 731; 25 R. 961; 76 S.
W. 845; Thierman Co. v. Wolff, 125 Ky . 832 ; 31
R. 376 ; 102 S. W. 843 .
Judgments ; foreign.- Statutesof thisstatemay
be reliedupon as a bar to an actionupon a foreign
judgment . McArthur v.Goddin , 12 Bush 274.
Lien is barred if debt is. French v . Bolling,
27 R. 639 ; 85 S. W. 1182 .
New promise or acknowledgment . " If not
paid, I request indulgence," indorsed on a note
by the obligorabout the time the note was exe-
cuted, did not stoptheobligorfrom pleading the
statute. If the new promise is made after the
statutorybar, the action must be upon the new
promise, if made before the action should be
upon the originalobligation. Carr v . Robinson ,
8 Bush 269; Marcum v. Terry, 146 Ky . 145; 142
S. W. 209 , and see note (34 ) §2515 .

an illegal arrest and assault will not stop the
running of the statute of limitations in favor

Rectanus , 32 R. 364, 105 S. W. 965 .
In an action against the administrator of a
maker of a note,the seven years'statuteof limita-
tion was pleaded and it was claimed that the
decedentwas a surety;absencefromthestatefor
a portionof the time was setup in the reply. The
jury was properlyinstructedthat ifthey believed
from the evidence that excluding the time the
decedent was absent from the state and the six
months followingthe appointment of the adminis-
trator, the time between the maturing of the
note and the filingof the action, did not amount
to as much as seven years, they should find for
plaintiff. Beavers' Admr . v. Ashlock, 156 Ky .
98, 160 S. W. 785.

S. W. 245 .

band's heirs to sue for the land ; but the repre-
sentation by the purchaser that he was claiming

If land be divided without a writing, continu-
ous possessionthereunder for fifteenyears willripen into a valid title. Blanton v. Howard , 148

A man conveyed property to his second wife

until the death of the woman entitled to

A surety on a note is released after seven years
from the accrual of the cause of action and a
payment whether made by himself or the principal
does not extend the period beyond that time .
Lillyv. Farmers'Nat.Bank , 22 R. 148,56 S. W.
722 .
A surety released by lapse of time under this
sectionisboundby a renewalnoteexecutedbyhim for the debt in consideration of an extension
of time to the principals. Steger v. Jackson, Sr.,
139 Ky . 491 , 31 R. 434 , 102 S. W. 329 .
The limitationof thissectionmust be pleaded,
and cannot be considered on a demurrer if the
petition simply shows that the time mentioned
in the statute has run . Brashears ' Heirs v . Brash-
ears, 144 Ky . 451 ; 139 S. W. 738 .
An action brought against the surety on the
bond of an assignee for the benefit of creditors
more than seven years after the right of action
accrued was barred by limitations. Neely v .
City Nat . Bank of Cairo, Ill., 150 Ky . 512, 150
S. W. 679 .
A surety may avail himself of this statute
although the plaintiffdid not know that he was
a surety. Morris v.Tydings,1 Ky .Opinions541.
A conversionby the sheriffof property in his
hands under an attachment is a breach of his
official bond . The cause of action of the attach-
ing creditor accrues when the attaching creditor
obtains his judgment in the attachment suit.
Coker v.Com .for the use of Powell , 3 Ky . Opinions
515 .
One who is reallya surety in a note but who
induces the owner of the note to believe that
he isa principaland a bailactionmay be estopped
frompleadingthissection. McElroyv. Dunn,5 Ky . Opinions 112 .
The provisions of this section are not invalid
as an unreasonable interferencewith the rights
of property . Dwiggins Wire Fence Co. v . Patter-
son , 166 Ky . 278 , 179 S. W. 224 .
Creditors of a decedent are barred of an action
against the suretieson the bond of his personal
representative in seven years after their cause
of action accrued . In a certain instance the cause
of action accrued when the commissioner of the

tain creditors of the decedent reported a settle-
ment and the amount of the balance in the hands
of the personalrepresentative. Com . v. Sammons ,
180 Ky . 403, 202 S. W. 885.
§ 2552. Surety; when provisionsof four
preceding sectionsdo not apply.- The lim-
itations given in the next four preceding
sections shallnot apply to so much of the
time elapsedwhen therewas no executor,
administrator or other person authorized
to commence an action, nor to the six
months during which an action can not be
brought againsta personalrepresentative;
nor to any delay assentedto by the surety,
in writing. And if judgment be rendered
for the plaintiff, in any case provided for
in those four sections, and the same be
afterward reversedor arrested,so thatthe
plaintifftakesnothingthereby,he may com-
mence another actionwithin one year there-
after. And if such surety shall abscond ,
concealhimself, or by removal from the
state, or otherwise, obstruct or hinder his
being sued, the time of such obstruction
shallnot be computed as part of the time of
limitationin saidsectionsallowed. And
ifsuch judgment be obstructedby appeal,
supersedeas,or injunction,the time of such
obstruction shall also be disallowed .
§ 2552. Absence from state.- Temporary ab-sence of debtor from country will not take a case
out of the statute. Ormsby v. Letcher, 3 Bibb 269;Menez v. Taylor, 91 Ky . 461; 13 R. 22; 16 S. W.128. But if, aftera permanent removal,the suretytemporarilyreturnsto the stateitwillnot prevent
the creditor from the benefit of the exception.
Bennett v. Devlin,17 B. M. 353; Ridgley v. Price,
16 В. М. 409 .
Assent to delay in writing . The act of the
suretyin signinga new note, which the principal
afterward refused to sign, can not in an action

Construction of first sentence of section . Davis

Obstruction or hindrance . If a surety verbally
asks for time and promises to pay the debt , and
the payee, relying upon such promise, forbears
to sue, this does not prevent limitation from run-
ning. Kennedy v.Foster, 14 Bush 479. Following
Coleman v. Walker , 3 Met . 65, and in effectover-
rulingthedictuminWalkerv.Sayers,5 Bush,579. A surety about the time the petition was
filedagreed with the creditorthat if he would
not sue on the note and save him any further
cost, he would , during the term of the court
which was in sessionwhen the petitionwas filed,confess judgment. The creditordelayed his suit
for twenty days under this agreement, when the
surety refused to confess judgment . The court

Newton v. Carson, 80 Ky . 309; 4 R. 1; and see
Hamilton v. Wright, 27 R. 1144; 87 S. W. 1093.
Unless the sureties acts are in point of fact

lation,an instructionin regardto the maintenance

ages caused thereby . Edwards ' Admx . v . Lam ,

tory duty of mine ventilation to a lessee who is

§2742. Authoritystrictlyconstrued.- General
rule is that the authoritydelegated to municipal
corporationsisto be strictlyconstrued. Kniper v .
Louisville, 7 Bush ,599; Wheatley v.Covington,11
Bush , 18; Johnston v. Louisville, 11 Bush , 527.
Exceptions to rule. Broadway Baptist Church v .
McAtee , 8 Bush , 508 .
City may hold property in trust under a will
for charitableuses, and may be compelled to
execute such trust. Peynado v. Peynado , 82 Ky
5 ; 5 R. 753 .
Discriminationagainst non -residents. A city
ordinance which discriminates against residents
of other states is in violation of the federal con-
stitution, although it makes the same discrimina-
tion against the residents of this state outside of
the city. Fecheimer v. Louisville, 84 Ky . 306; 8
R. 310 ; 2 S. W. 65 .
Issual and sale of municipal bonds . It is no
objectionto an ordinance providingfor the issual
of municipal bonds that it gives the mayor the
discretion to sell them at a lower rate of inter-
est than that fixed in the ordinance if he can do
80 . There is no unauthorizeddelegationof legis-
lative power . Frantz v. Jacob , 88 Ky . 525 ; 11
R. 55 ; 11 S. W. 654 .
Legislativepower.- General councilcan not,by
contract, deprive itselfof this power . Lou . City
Ry . v . Louisville, 8 Bush , 415 .
Market ; regulation of.- Mayor and council
havethepowertoinflictpenaltiespenaltiesonitscitizens
for vending at market articlesnot the product of
the vendor. Louisvillev.Roupe ,6 B. М. 591.
Nuisance ; abatement of.- City government
may , when the use to which the owner devotes
his property becomes a nuisance , compel him to
cease to use it, and punish him for refusing to
obey its ordinances . Lou . City Ry . v . Louisville, 8
Bush , 415 .
Observance of Sabbath .- Enforcement of ob-
servance of Sabbath ; powers of city. Ormsby v .
Louisville, 79 Ky . 197 ; 2 R. 297 .
Ordinance fixing offense and punishment . The
mayor and councilhave the right, by theirordi-
nance , to define the acts which they intend to
punish,and theactdefinedistheoffense. Louis-
villev.Roupe, 6 B. M. 591.
Penal Ordinances . A general grant of power
should not be held to confer authority upon a
municipal corporationto make an ordinance pun-
ishing an act which is made punishable as a crim-
inal offense by the state laws . Com . v . Duff , 87
Ky .586; 10 R. 617; 9 S.W. 816.

itiesentrusted with the power may make contracts
to attain this end ; and when made they can not

The mayor can not,as a generalrule,employ coun-

Special privileges.- A statute enacted for the

State laws operate within the limits of muni-

Liabilities of Corporation
Injunction by city taxpayer .- A city taxpayer
may enjoin the issuingof illegalbonds by the
city, both for his own protectionand for that
of innocent parties who may purchase them .
Frantz v. Jacob, 88 Ky . 525; 11 R. 55; 11 S. W.
654 .
Mandamus against city council.- Jurisdiction
of Jeffersoncircuitcourt. Kaye v. Kean , 18 B.
M. 839. Mandamus lies against city council to
compel the levy and collection of a tax to pay
bonds issued to a railroad company . Maddox v .
Graham , 2 Met . 56; Fleming v. Dyer , 20 R. 689;
47 S. W. 444 .
Negligence of fireman .-City being required to
establish and maintain a fire department , is, not
liablefor injuriescaused by the negligence of
fireman. Greenwood v . Louisville, 13 Bush , 226 .
Negligence of policeman.- City not liable for
wilful negligence of policemen in making arrest
upon charge of felony. They act as officersof the
commonwealth . Pollockv.Louisville,13 Bush ,221.
Officialmisconduct of officers.- City officersare
responsible for malfeasance or nonfeasance in
office, but the corporationis not liablefor official
misconduct of itsofficers. Prather v. Lexington,
13 В. М. 557 ; Ward v . Louisville, 16 В. М. 184 ;
nor for wilful neglect of policemen . Pollock v .
Louisville, 13 Bush 221 .
Propertydestroyedby mob .- Citynot responsi-ble. Prather v . Lexington , 13 B. M. 557 ; Ward
v . Louisville, 16 B. M. 184 ; but now by statute
under certain restrictionsthe city is liable. See
§8 and notes .
Recovery of money paid by mistake . One who
has paid money to a city,under a mistaken belief
as to the validity of an ordinance which required
the money to be paid for a license to do business,
may recover the money , the ordinance being in.
valid. Fecheimer v. Louisville, 84 Ky . 306; 8 R.
310 ; 2 S. W. 65 .
Taxation of city property ; exemption . See con .,

A city council may by ordinance punish acts
which are offenses at common law . City of Louis-
villev. Wehmhoff , 116 Ky . 812, 25 R. 995, 76 S.
W. 876 .

the benefitof a contractor's work in reconstructing
a street does not create a contract by implication

City of Newport v . Schoolfield, 142 Ky . 287 ; 134

struct a sidewalk fifteen feet wide , of which the
middle third was of cement or artificialstone, and
five feet on each side was solid ground , and to
assess the entire cost against the abutting prop-
erty. Holmes v . Heeter & Son , 146 Ky . 52 ; 142
S. W. 210 .
This section and §§ 3096-3102 are not violative
of const., § 51, relating to subjects of acts. Mulli-
gan v . McGregor , 165 Ky . 222 ; 176 S. W. 1129 .

where two streetswere opened for public use
in connectionwith the saleof lots, and remained
open for twenty years subject to continual and
uninterruptedpublicuser, although not improved.

1129 .

gan v.McGregor , 165 Ky . 222; 176 S. W. 1129.

§ 3359. Jurisdiction; punishment .- Police courts
have exclusive jurisdiction of all prosecutions for
violations of ordinances and by -laws of the city.
For a common law offense not punishable under
any statutean ordinancemay fixa lesspenaltythan the common law . City of Owensboro v .
Simms , 99 Ky . 49 ; 17 R. 1393 ; 34 S. W. 1085. An
ordinance may fixa higher,but can not fixa lower
penalty for a statutory offense than does the
statute . City of Owensboro v . Sparks , 99 Ky . 351 ;
18 R. 269; 36 S. W. 4; and see Taylor v. City of
Owensboro ,98 Ky .271; 17 R. 856; 32 S. W. 948;holding that an ordinance prescribinga lesspen-
alty thanthe statuteisvoid. In Com .v. Hunter,19 R. 1109; 41 S.W. 284,itisheld that the circuit
court has concurrentjurisdictionwith the police
court,of offensescommitted in the citywhen the
offenseispunishableat common law or under a
statute, although the city have an ordinance pun-
ishing the offense.
Disorderly conduct is a distinct offense from
a breach of the peace , and the penalty imposed for
it may be fixed by ordinance in any sum . City v .
Holly, 108 Ky . 621; 22 R. 358; 57 S. W. 491.

§ 3588. Board of education may maintain man-
damus proceedings against city council to compel
it to pay money to which board is entitled. City
v . Board of Education , 21 R. 731 ; 52 S. W. 969 .
School elections . Members of the board of
education must be elected by a viva voce vote ,
and allpersons who may vote under the general
school law (§4434 ) are entitled to vote at the
election. Moss v . Riley, 19 R. 993 ; 43 S. W. 421 ;
102 Ky . 1 ; but in City v . Board of Education , 21
R. 731 ; 52 S. W. 969 ; it is held that although
board of education was elected by secret ballot
the election was valid, as there was no contest
and no complaint about itsfairness, and see Elliott
v . Burke , 113 Ky . 479 ; 24 R. 292 ; 68 S. W. 445,
holding that an election of the board of education
by secret ballot is void . See , further, as to school
elections. Trustees v . Stone , 142 Ky . 715 ; 135
S. W. 307 .
SEYMOUR'S NOTES
Under this section the board of education of
a city of the fourth class is charged with the
conduct of the common schools and entrusted with
the control of the school funds . The board joined
with the city authoritiesin callingelectionsto
levy an increasedtax for schoolpurposes, under
§3490 , to issue bonds for school purposes , and to
set aside part of the income of the board to pay
interest on the bonds and redeem them . The board
also joined with the city authoritiesin issuing
the bonds . None of these acts affecttheir validity.
Bowman v. City of Middlesboro, 28 R. 1290; 91
S. W. 726 .
A cityof the sixthclass,being part of a graded
school district, was made a city of the fourth
class and the city council created a board of educa-
tion. As against the trustees of a graded school
district, the board was entitled to the possession
of the school property within the city. Trustees
of Latonia Graded School District No 12 v . Board
ef Education of Latonia , 29 R. 391 ; 93 S. W. 590 .
A vacancy in a school board occuring in April,
1910 , was properly filledby appointment until the
general November election, 1911. Hollar v. Cor-
nett, 144 Ky . 420 ; 138 S. W. 298 ; Hollar v . Allen ,
144 Ky . 420 ; 138 S. W. 298.
Injunction is a proper proceeding to prevent
persons who are wrongfully claiming to be mem-
bers of a board of education from exercising any
of the duties of that office; but in the injunction
proceedingthe questionof eligibilityof one of the
defendants cannot be raised. Hollar v . Cornett ,
144 Ky . 420 ; 138 S. W. 298; Hollar v . Allen, 144
Ky . 420 ; 138 S. W. 298 .
Trustees who should have qualifiedon the first
Monday in January qualified on the next day
thereafter; a treasurerelectedby them couldnot
be ousted by reason of this delay. The court
further says that they were de jure officers. Jewett
v .Matteson ,148 Ky . 820; 147 S. W. 924.

By an Act of March 26 , 1904 , с. 126 , p . 311 , " An
act to amend and re -enact $ 4348 of the
Kentucky statues," § 1 of the Act of 1893 was amended
not only as to the purposes for which private passways ,
tram roads , haul roads , etc., might be opened , but pro-
cedure for enforcing the right was laid down . (See
Fitzpatrick v . Warden , 157 Ky . 95 , 162 S. W. 550 ,
and cases there cited for a construction of the Act of
1904.)
By an Act of March , 1918 , с. 99 , p . 439 , the
legislaturere-enacted the provisions of the Act of 1893
without any change whatsoever except the addition of
thewords " (a regular steamboat landing) ," making no
referencein any form to the Act of 1893 nor to the Act
of 1904. The title to the Act of 1918 was , " An acttoprovide for the opening of private passways ." Con-
struing the action of the legislature as expressed in the
saidActs of 1893 , 1904 and 1918 , the editor was of the
opinion that the Act of 1918 " covers the whole subject
of the former one and is manifestly intended as a sub-
stitutefor it" (see Exall v . Holland , supra ), and the
Act of 1904 was , therefore , believed to have been re-
pealed. See editorial note to § 3779a -1 in Volume 3
(1918) of the Kentucky statutes, 1915 edition.
Act of 1918 was accordingly compiled as the law . The
Actof1918 provided sectionheadingsin the languageof
thoseemployed in the 1909 editionof the Kentuckystatutes.

ment to take it outside of the state for storage

This section is not invalid for uncertainty , be-
cause real value means market value, which is

common law by doing away with the necessityof

dient of the offense . Com . v . International Har-

in so far as it secures to farmers the real value
of their products, but is invalidin so far as it
enables them to get more than the real value
therefor . Nor is it in violation of the fourteenth
amendment of the federal constitution . This sec-
tion taken with the fourteenth amendment of the
federal constitution amends §3915 so as to give
others the same pooling rights as farmers . Com .
v . International Harvester Co., 131 Ky . 551 , 767 ;
115 S. W. 703 .
The essence of the offense under this section
and §3915 since the act of March 21, 1906, is
the raising or lowering of the price of any article
above or below its real value . Am . Tobacco Co.
v. Com ..132 Ky . 115 S. W. 754; 116 S. W. 1176.
By act of March 8, 1910 (S. A., p. 29), lists
of persons pledging farm products may be re-corded . The statute prescribes the effect of
records and makes the purchase of property
pledged and embraced in the recorded list an
offense .
By act of 1910 (S. A., p. 343), the right to
pool farm products is enlarged.
By act of 1910 (S. A., p. 339),growers of farm
products may agree to abstainfrom growing anykind of crops for a given periodor season.
This section is not in conflict with the federal
anti-trust act of July 2, 1890, known as the Sher-
man law . Com .v.Hodges, 137 Ky .233; 125 S. W.
689 .

had a lien on the other half sold the tobacco with-
out the knowledge or consent of the owner of the
other half. It did not bring enough to satisfy the
lien . The one -half which was under lien had been
pooled; and the person so pooling it ratifiedthe
sale. He was not guilty of violating this section.
Cook v . Com ., 141 Ky . 439 ; 132 S. W. 1032 .
A person who bought a crop of tobacco which
he bad not himself raised, but which had been
pooled, sold the same in violationof the pooling
contract . He did not by such sale violate this
section. Com . v. Malone, 141 Ky . 441; 132 S. W.
1033 .
Subsection 3 (act of March 13, 1908, S. A. P.
38) is not in conflictwith $ 51 of the constitution.

A pooling contract was made in a certain

the article upon which it fixes a price. Inter-
national Harvester Co of Am . v . Com ., 144 Ky .

cient to sustain a conviction . International Har-

The formation of trusts or monopolies is not

if they sell their products above or below their

SEYMOUR'S NOTES
By act of March 18, 1912 (S. A., p. 391), the
revenue agent system is greatly modified.
Under this section and § 4260 , suits to assess
omitted property and collect taxes thereon must
be brought in the name of the state on relation
of the sheriff or revenue agent , and not by the
auditor of state. Com . v. Helm , 163 Ky . 69 ; 173
S. W. 389 .
Under this section and §§ 4259 and 4260 a
revenue agent can not take an appeal after the
expirationof his term of office, and such appeal
will be dismissed . Com . v . Columbia Trust Co.,
162 Ky . 825 ; 173 S. W. 386.
A proceeding for the assessment of omitted
property isa specialproceeding, and the judge of
the county court in assessing the property, acts in
a ministerial capacity. Stearns Coal & Lumber
Co. v . Com ., 167 Ky . 51 ; 179 S. W. 1080 .
An actionmay be brought by the commonwealth
for the collection of an inheritance tax if it be
approved by the supervisor of revenue agents .
Sevier's Extx . v . Commonwealth , 181 Ky . 49 ; 203
S. W. 1070 .
The state tax commission may remove a revenue
agent without cause or hearing . Simons v . Scott ,
188 Ky . 535 ; 222 S. W. 1075 .

§ 4370. School fund . It was held under con-
stitution of 1850, substantially like present con-
stitution (§184 ), that the school fund must be
used exclusively in aid of the common schools, and
an act appropriatinga part of the school fund
to purchase Collins' History of Kentucky was
held unconstitutional. Collins v . Henderson , 11
Bush , 74 .
The legislaturehas power to pass laws regu-
lating the manner in which the common school
fund shall be devoted to the purposes for which
it was set apart, but these laws should be general
in their application. Halbert v. Sparks, 9 Bush ,
259 ; Auditor v . Holland , 14 Bush , 147 .
The general assembly has no power to abdicate
its control over the school fund and give to the
county courts, to be performed at their pleasure,
the power which the constitution vested alone in
the legislature. 14 Bush , 147 .
It was held in Auditor v . Trustees , 81 Ky . 680 ;
5 R. 797 , that no part of the taxes collected from
railroads should be applied to the school fund , but
this section has changed the law under which that
decision was rendered .
Construction of section. Fuqua v . Superintend-
ent, P. Ins., 119 Ky . 407 ; 27 R. 46 ; 84 S. W. 325 .

§ 4675. Acts constituting survey . The acts
legallydone on the groundby the surveyorcon-

Allowance for variation. Surveys can not be

Exceptions to surveyor's report.-Reports of

magneticmeridian; the variationof the needleis

Return of plat and certificate. It is not essen-
tial to the validity of a patent that the plat and
certificate should have been filed within six months
from the date of the survey . Goosling v . Smith ,
90 Ky . 157 ; 11 R. 991 ; 13 S. W. 437 .
Return of survey to land office. While the in-
choate right to land acquired by a survey is not
lost by failing to return the survey to the land
officewithin the time prescribed by statute, and
the holder of the survey may , notwithstanding
such failure,stillobtain a grant vestinghim with
titlefrom the time of itsissual,yet this right must
be perfected within a reasonable time . A survey
made in 1853 , on which no patent was issued, was
barred in 1888 by laches of the holder. Bryant
v . Wood , 90 Ky . 530 ; 12 R. 454; 14 S. W. 498 .
Rules in aid of recovery of lost lines and cor-
ners. In general distance must yield to courses.
The beginning corner is of no higher dignity than
any other corner. It is lawful to begin at any
corner of the survey and to reverse the succession
of lines. If there is uncertainty in a certificate,
the construction most against the party claiming
under it must prevail. Pearson v . Baker , 4 Dana ,
221. When visible land -marks fail resort is to be

Beckley v .Bryan , Snd . 91 ; Bryan v . Beckley , Litt.
Sel. Cas., 91; Thornberry v. Churchill, 4 Mon. 29.
Where it is evident that distance is the material
and intended to be the controlling call, course
must yield to it. Blight v . Atwell , 4 J. J. M. 278 .
Surveyor's report evidence of any fact and of

§ 4679e-4. **Railroad commission given jurisdiction.**—The railroad commission shall have jurisdiction of the matters set out in § 4679e-3 of this act and shall keep a record of its acts in relation thereto to be entered in the minutes of said commission. (Id., § 2.)

§ 4679f-1. **Interchange and transmission of messages.**—Telephone companies operating exchanges in different towns and cities shall receive and transmit each other's messages without unreasonable delay or discrimination, and the telephone exchange receiving any message from the exchange in which said message originated shall in the event the destination of said message be an exchange or point beyond the lines of the exchange first receiving it as above stated then said exchange first receiving said message and the exchanges connected therewith through which said message should be routed, shall switch said message through their respective exchanges by causing without unreasonable delay or discrimination and with the same promptness with which messages originating and ending on their own lines are handled, the talking circuit to be connected up over the toll line leading through or from said receiving exchange through other connecting exchanges to the point of destination.

In order to give effect to § 199 of the constitution it is hereby intended to cover the connecting up and usage of toll lines through the various intervening exchanges between the exchange in which the message originate and the point of destination so that the party requesting said service shall be able to hold a conversation over the telephone circuit with the party called at the point of destination.

(Act of July 6 ,1893 )
TURNPIKE , GRAVEL AND PLANK ROADS
* By Section 89 of an Act of March 23 , 1914 , с . 80 , р .
338 , now Section 4356s of the Kentucky Statutes , Sec-
tions 4712-4748c , all inclusive and Chapter 110 of Acts
of 1910 , were expressly repealed . The title to this Act
was " An act defining public roads ; providing for their
establishment , regulation , use and maintenance ; and cre-
ating the officeof county road engineer , and prescribingthe duties thereof." This title is practically identical
with the titleof the repealed act of March 18 , 1912 , с.
110 , p . 309. Said act of 1914 now form Sections 4287 ,
et seq., of the Kentucky Statutes, 1915 edition.
Sections 39 and 40 of the act of 1912 are practically
identical with Sections 30 and 31 , respectively , of the
Act of 1914 , now Sections 4316 and 4317 of the Ken-
tucky Statutes , 1915 edition .
In the case of Burton v . Monticello and Burnside
Turnpike Co., 162 Ky . 787 , 173 S. W. 144 , the Court
of Appeals held that the subject of toll roads was not
included within the subject expressed in the title of the
Act of 1912 , and , therefore , Sections 39 and 40 were
unconstitutional . For the reasons given in that case it
is concluded that the corresponding Sections 30 and 31 of
the Act of 1914 , Kentucky Statutes. Sections 4316 and
4317 , are unconstitutional .
As the subject of " toll roads " was not included in
the title of the Act of 1912 , the Court of Appeals also
held in the above case, Sections 39 and 40 of the
Act , being unconstitutional , did not have the effect of
repealing Section 4724 of the 1909 edition of the Ken-
tucky Statutes , relating to toll charges .
In the case of Houston v . Boltz , Judge , 169 Ky . 640 ,
185 S. W. 76 , the Court of Appeals was called upon to
consider the effect of the title of the Act of 1914 , and
on the authority of Burton v . Monticello , etc., supra ,
the court held that the subject of toll roads was not
included in said Act , for which reason so much of
Section 89 thereof , now Sections 4356s of the 1915
edition of the Kentucky Statutes, as attempted to repeal
Sections 4712-4748c of the 1909 edition was unconstitu-
tional and void and that Section 4748b of the 1909
edition was still in effect.Both of the foregoing cases were decided after the
publication of the 1915 edition of the Kentucky Stat-
utes and , therefore, have the effectof replacing the whole
of Chapter 129 of the 1909 edition referring to private
or to quasi -public roads .

§ 4768. Definition of warehouseman .- This stat-

CHAPTER 135

WILLS
§4824. Will; meaning ofword .- Except
where itwould be contrary to the manifest
intention, the word " will," as used in this
chapter, shall signify a last will or testa-
ment , codicil, appointment by will, or writ-
ing in the nature of a will in exercise of a
power , and also any other testamentary
disposition.
§ 4824. Acceptance of devise ; estoppel. The
acceptance by a devisee, who was a married
woman , of a check sent her in payment of the
devise did not , under the circumstances of this
case, estop her from contesting will. Hicks v .
Smith, 12 R. 976; 16 S. W. 91; White v. Mayhall,
15 R. 830 ; 25 S. W. 881 .
When a devisee accepts property devised to
him he thereby relinquisheshis right to property
of his own which the testator has undertaken to
devise to another. McQuerry v. Gilliland, 89 Ky .
434 ; 11 R. 656 ; 12 S. W. 1037 ; Brossenne v.
Schmitt , 91 Ky . 465 ; 13 R. 26 ; 16 S. W. 135 ;
Huhlein v. Huhlein, 87 Ky . 247; 10 R. 107; 8
S. W. 260 .
If one accepts a benefit under a will he must
adopt the entire instrument and renounce every
rightinconsistentwith it. Brossenne v.Schmitt,91
Ky . 465 ; 13 R. 26 ; 16 S. W. 135 ; Kellar v . Stanley ,
86 Ky . 240 ; 9 R. 388 ; 5 S. W. 477 .
Agreement not to contest a will in considera-
tion of a certain sum is enforcible. Waller v .
Marks , 100 Ky . 541; 19 R. 121; 38 S. W. 894.
Ambiguity . The facts and circumstances sur-
rounding the testator at the time of the execution
of the will and bearing in any way thereon, arecompetent to be considered when there is am-
biguityor uncertaintyof meaning in the language
used by the testator. Henry v. Henry , 81 Ky .
342; 5 R. 283; see, further, as to competency ofparol evidence to explain ambiguities, Stephens v.Walker , 8 B. M. 601 ; Fogle v. Fogle, 9 Bush , 721;Timberlake v. Parrish, 5 Dana , 346; Mitchell v.
Walker, 17 B. M. 62; Haydon v. Ewing, 1 B. M.111; Breckinridge v. Duncan , 2 Mar. 51.
Burden of proof ; argument . Milton v . Hunter ,
13 Bush , 163 ; Flood v . Pragoff, 79 Ky . 607; 3 R.
372; Singleton'sWill, 8 Dana , 315; Rogers v.Thomas, 1 B. M. 390; Hawkins v. Grimes, 13
B. M. 257; Howat v. Howat , 19 R. 756; 41 S.W.
771; Bottom v. Bottom, 32 R. 494; 106 S. W.216; Bramel v. Bramel, 101 Ky . 64; 18 R. 1074;
39 S.W. 520; Woodford v.Buckner, 111 Ky . 241;23 R. 627; 63 S. W. 617; Boone v. Richie, 21 R.
864; 53 S. W. 518; Folks v. Folks, 107 Ky . 561;21 R. 1275; 54 S. W. 837; Willsv. Farmer, 19 R.
795 ; 39 S. W. 422 ; and see § 4850 .
Capacity to make will exists " when the testa-
tor has mind and memory enough to understand
thathe isselectingthe personswhom he wishes
tohave hispropertyand to know hisproperty,and the naturalobjectsof hisbounty, and hisdutiesto them and the personsupon whom hisproperty is bestowed by the testamentary paper
whichhe signs." Wise v. Foote, 81 Ky . 10; 4
R. 643; Tudor v. Tudor, 17 B. M. 383; and see
Woodford v. Buckner, 111 Ky . 241; 23 R. 627;
63 S. W. 617 ; Rasdall v . Brush , 31 R. 1138 ; 104
S. W. 749; Bottom v. Bottom, 32 R. 494; 106
S. W. 216 .
It is not essential that the testator's mind and
memory should be as good as they had ever been .
Nor are occasional fitsof intemperance or want of
domestic management or general bad conduct suffi-
cient to show want of capacity. Harper's Will,
4 Bibb , 244 .
To make a valid will although the testator must
be of sound disposing mind and memory , every
mental defect will not incapacitate, but where the
impairment of mind is caused by old age it is
stronger evidence of incapacity than other species
of mental infirmitiesaccompanied by lucid inter-
vals. Turner v . Turner , 1 Litt. 101.
Where a testatorisapparentlyof sound mindexcept in regard to certain things, and manifests
such an unfounded and unnatural aversion for his
relatives as to show that, concerning them , his
mind is not right, he is incapable of making a
will. Johnson v . Moore , 1 Litt. 371 .
That a will was written by the testator and
itsprovisions altogether sensible, proper and judi-
cious, is to be regarded as the best evidence of
capacityat the time the willwas made . Overton
v . Overton , 18 B. M. 61 ; Weir's Will, 9 Dana , 434 .
Wills may be establishedagainstthe testimony
of the attesting witnesses who testify that testa-
tor did not have sufficientcapacity to make a will.Alsey Howard's Will, 5 Mon. 199; and see
MeMeekin v . McMeekin , 2 Bush , 79 ; Hoerth v .
Zable , 92 Ky . 202 ; 13 R. 470 ; 17 S. W. 360.
Where a testator's mind has for some time
prior to his death been deranged, with occasional
lucid intervals, it ought to be shown by clear and
satisfactory evidence that the will was made
during a lucid interval. Cochran's Will , 1 Mon.
263 .
Paralysis of the body for several years before
death does not necessarilyaffectthe mind , and
although a testator may not be able to walk , or
at times to talk plain, he may have sufficientca-
pacityto make a will. McDaniel's Will,2 J.J.M.
331 .
Intellectualfeebleness alone does not disqualify
a person from making a willunlessthe weakness
is of such extent that the dispositon of his estate
bears evidence of a deranged understanding .
Elliott'sWill , 2 J. J. M. 340 .
Charitable or humane purpose ; devise for. Ford
v . Ford , 91 Ky . 572 ; 13 R. 183 ; 16 S. W. 451 ;
Spalding v.St.Joseph'sInd.School, 107 Ky . 382;
21 R. 1107; 54 S. W. 200; and see notes to charit-
able uses, § 317.
Children; right to disinherit.- A testatorof
sound mind , and not unduly influenced, may dis-
pose of his property as he pleases, and may dis-
inherit one or all of his children, or devise the
whole of his estate to any one of them . Hoerth

Codicil; change in will.- The disposition of
property by a will is not disturbed by an erroneous
recitalof itscontentsin a codicil, unlessa design

Conditionalwills, as to when writings dispos-
ing of estatein the event of certaincontingencies,
such as that the testator should not return alive
from an expected visit, or a fatal accident should
happen to him during his absence from home ,
will be regarded as valid wills. See Likefield v .

25; Massie v. Griffin, 2 Met . 364; Urey v. Urey ,
86 Ky . 354; 9 R. 596; 5 S. W. 859; Pelley v .

Conditional devise ; trust estate ; creditors.-
Where a testator devised in trust the income of
certainproperty to his son for life, but provided
that if the court decided that it might be sub-
jected to the payment of the debts of the son,
then the trustee should thereafter pay the income
to the wife of the son, the creditors could only
subject the income up to the time the court held
that itcould be subjected. Bull v.Ky .Nat .Bank ,
90 Ky . 452 ; 12 R. 536 ; 14 S. W. 425 .
Construction .- All the parts of a will should be
made to harmonize,ifitcan be done without doing
violence to its provisions, and the intention of the
testator is to be gathered from the whole will.
Daniel v.Thompson ,14 B. M. ,662; Moran v.Dille-
hay, 8 Bush , 434; effectshould be given as far as
practicable to every part of the will. Baird v .
Rowan ,1 Mar. 217; Morse v. Cross,17 В. М. 735.
Intentionof the testatoristhe governing prin-
ciplein theconstructionof wills. Webb v.Webb ,
12 В. М. 47; and the testator's intention must be
gathered from allthe provisionsof the will. Wil-
liamson v. Williamson, 18 B. M. 329; Augustus v .
Seabolt, 3 Met . 156; Anderson v. Hall, 80 Ky .91;
3 R. 579; Bayless v.Prescott,79 Ky . 252; 2 R. 262.
The language of wills is to be construed ac-
cording to common intendment ; technical rules of
construction will not be allowed to defeat the in-
tention. Moore v. Moore , 12 B. M. 656; Allen v .
Vanmeter , 1 Met . 277; Cromie v. Orphans ' Home ,
3 Bush , 365 .
Supplying, transposing or rejectingwords is
allowable , if necessary to effectuate the intention

§ 4888. Construction of § 4888.- The intended
operation of the Kentucky act is very clear in
regard to injuries received outside of this state
under contracts of employment made here . Unless
the employer and employee agree in writing to
exempt themselves from the operation of this
statute, then the remedies provided by this law
are exclusiveon claims made in thisstateby the
employee, for injuriesreceivedout of it. As was
said by the court in Deeny v . Wright & Cobb
Lighterage Co., 36 N. J. L. J. 121; 7 N. C. C. A.,
note 144 : " The statute can have no extraterri-
torial effect, but it can require a contract to be
made , by two partiesto a hiring, that the con-
*

tract shall have an extraterritorial effect. The
contract is binding on the employee himself and
upon the employer, and it is conclusivelypre-
sumed that the parties have accepted the provi
sions of § 2 and have agreed to be bound thereby .
It would seem that the reasonable con-
struction of the statute is, that it writes into the
contractof employment certainadditionalterms.
The cause of action of the petitioner is ex con-
tractu. The lex loci contractus governs the con-

and not the " lex loci deliciti" as was formerly

Effect of settlement by employee with third per-
sons. This act does not provide what the effect
shall be when an employee having a claim both
against the employer for compensation and a third
person for damages , settles the claim with the
third person . The employer is made liable under
the act, for the benefit of the employee , for in-
juriescaused by thirdpersons, but the employer
has the right to seek reimbursement for the
amount paid out from the person who is legallyliablefor the injury. Therefore when an em-
ployee settleswith such third person without the
employer's consent he is depriving the employer
of the right given him by the act to seek full
indemnity for the compensation for which the law
makes him liable . It has therefore been held that
the acceptance of such a settlement with a third
person whose negligence caused the injury is a
bar to a claim for compensation against the em-
ployer. Cripps ' Case , 216 Mass . 586 ; 104 N. E.
565 ; Ann . Cas . 1915B , 828 ; Page v. Burtwell , 2
K. B. (Eng .) 758 ; L. R. A. 1916A (note ), 361.
In the Cripps Case (supra) a driver of a truck
was injured by the negligence of a street car com-
pany . It was held that he losthis rightto com-
pensation by settling with the company although
he had not brought suit against them . But in the
same case it was held when he later died of these
injuriesthat his widow was not by his settlement
deprived of her rightto compensation. See § 44f
and compare with Louisville Ry . Co. v . Raymond's
Admr ., 135 Ky . 738; 123 S. W. 281. The settle-
ment is a bar although in making it the workman

employer .' ''
